title.zh: 卷三百八十七 列傳第一百四十六 黃洽 汪應辰 王十朋 吳芾 陳良翰 杜莘老
title.en: Volume 387 Biographies 146: Huang Qia, Wang Yingchen, Wang Shipeng, Wu Fei, Chen Lianghan, Du Shenlao
title.raw: 卷三百八十七 列傳第一百四十六 黃洽 汪應辰 王十朋 吳芾 陳良翰 杜莘老 Volume 387 Biographies 146: Huang Qia, Wang Yingchen, Wang Shipeng, Wu Fei, Chen Lianghan, Du Shenlao

sentences.zh: 黃洽，字德潤，福州候官人。

translations.literal: Huang Qia, styled Derun, was a native of Houguan in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Qia, whose style name was Derun, was a native of Houguan in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，以太學生試春官第二，詔循故事，未臨軒，賜第二人及第。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing, as a student of the Imperial Academy he placed second in the spring civil examination; following precedent, before the palace audience he was granted jinshi status as the second-ranked candidate.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Longxing reign, as a student of the Imperial Academy he placed second in the spring civil examination; following precedent, before the palace audience he was granted jinshi status as the second-ranked candidate.

sentences.zh: 授紹興府觀察判官。

translations.literal: He was appointed Investigation Adjutant of Shaoxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigation adjutant of Shaoxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，就銓選，不用前名例謁廟堂。

translations.literal: When his term expired he sought selection in the roster and did not follow the former-rank precedent in paying court at the Office Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he sought appointment through the roster and did not follow the usual practice of using his former examination rank to pay court at the Office Hall.

sentences.zh: 宰相陳俊卿白於上，改宣義郎，除國子博士。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Chen Junqing informed the emperor; Qia was changed to Gentleman for Extending Righteousness and appointed Erudite of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Chen Junqing informed the emperor, and Qia was given the rank of Gentleman for Extending Righteousness and appointed erudite of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 適有旨職事官無待次，改差浙東安撫司主管機宜文字。

translations.literal: Just then an order came that functional officials need not await their turn in the roster; he was reassigned as Planning Secretary on the staff of the Eastern Zhejiang Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: An order had just been issued that officeholders need not wait their turn in the appointment queue; he was reassigned as chief planning secretary on the Eastern Zhejiang Pacification Commission staff.

sentences.zh: 繼為太學國子博士，樞密院編修官，通判福州。

translations.literal: He successively served as Erudite of the Imperial College and Directorate of Education, Compilation Officer in the Bureau of Military Affairs, and Vice Prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to serve as Erudite of the Imperial College and Directorate of Education, as a compilation officer in the Bureau of Military Affairs, and as vice prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 奉祠，召為太常丞。

translations.literal: He took leave for temple service, then was summoned as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After a period of temple leave, he was recalled and appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 請外，孝宗方厲精求治，曰：「黃洽厚德，方任以事。」

translations.literal: He requested an outside post; Emperor Xiaozong was then vigorously pursuing good governance and said: "Huang Qia possesses deep virtue and is just being entrusted with affairs."
translations.idiomatic: When he asked to leave the capital for an outside post, Emperor Xiaozong—who was then vigorously pursuing good governance—said, "Huang Qia is a man of deep virtue, and I have only just begun to entrust him with real responsibilities."

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: [The request] was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 當對，奏三事：備事莫若儲才，士卒當練其心，軍政必預為謀。

translations.literal: When he appeared for audience, he memorialized on three matters: to prepare for events nothing surpasses storing up talent; soldiers' hearts must be trained; military affairs must be planned in advance.
translations.idiomatic: At an imperial audience he presented three points: the best preparation for any contingency is to stockpile talent; soldiers must have their hearts trained; and military policy must be planned well ahead of time.

sentences.zh: 上矍然，洽徐奏：「願戒飭州郡，毋煩擾以致寇，毋輕易以玩寇。

translations.literal: The emperor started; Qia then slowly added: "I wish to admonish that prefectures and commanderies must not harass the people and thereby invite bandits, nor treat matters lightly and thereby invite contempt from bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started at this; Qia then went on more slowly: "I urge Your Majesty to warn prefectures and commanderies not to harass the people and thereby breed rebellion, and not to treat threats lightly and thereby invite contempt from rebels.

sentences.zh: 寇擾而後定，傷根本多矣。」

translations.literal: To pacify only after bandits have already risen causes far more damage to the root [of the state]."
translations.idiomatic: To restore order only after rebels have already run riot does far more harm to the foundations of the state."

sentences.zh: 繇秘書郎遷著作郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted from Gentleman of the Secretariat to Gentleman for Compilation.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted from gentleman of the Secretariat to gentleman for compilation.

sentences.zh: 上諭詞臣：「秘閣儲英俊為異時公卿用，行黃洽詞，可及之。」

translations.literal: The emperor instructed the drafting officials: "The Secret Cabinet stores outstanding men for use as grand ministers in future times; in composing Huang Qia's credentials, you may reach that standard."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the drafting officials, "The Secret Cabinet holds outstanding men for future service as chief ministers; in drafting Huang Qia's appointment text, you may aim at that level."

sentences.zh: 除右正言，首奏：「諫臣非具員，職在諫爭，朝政有闕，所當盡言。」

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Remonstrator and at once memorialized: "Remonstrators are not mere quota posts; their duty is remonstrance and dispute. Where court governance falls short, they should speak fully."
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Right Remonstrator, he opened with a memorial: "Censors are not mere headcount posts—their duty is to remonstrate. Where court policy falls short, they must speak out fully."

sentences.zh: 上亦以為端士，許其盡言無隱。

translations.literal: The emperor also regarded him as an upright man and permitted him to speak fully without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor likewise took him for an upright man and allowed him to speak his mind without reserve.

sentences.zh: 除侍御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed attending censor.

sentences.zh: 會水旱頻仍，因祠祭上言：「此事全在一念，陛下夙興默想，專精在民，身雖法宮，心則壇壝，洋洋左右，理非漠然。

translations.literal: As floods and droughts recurred, on the occasion of a sacrificial rite he submitted: "This matter rests entirely in a single thought: Your Majesty rises early and reflects in silence, concentrating your mind on the people. Though your person is in the imperial palace, your heart is at the altar; all around you, principle is not indifferent.
translations.idiomatic: Floods and droughts came in succession; taking advantage of a state sacrifice, he said, "This all turns on a single resolve: if Your Majesty rises early and reflects in silence, fixing your mind wholly on the people, then though your body remains in the palace, your heart stands at the altar—and the spirit that surrounds you cannot be indifferent to their plight.

sentences.zh: 洊歲荒歉之由，必有未盡契神示之心者。」

translations.literal: The reason for repeated years of famine and dearth must be that something has not yet fully accorded with what the spirits intend to show."
translations.idiomatic: The reason famine has returned year after year must be that something in our conduct has not yet fully answered what Heaven is trying to show us."

sentences.zh: 一日特詔：「諸路奉行荒政不虔，差官按視安集。」

translations.literal: One day a special edict came: "The circuits are not devout in carrying out famine relief; dispatch officials to inspect and settle the people."
translations.idiomatic: One day a special edict declared, "The circuits are not carrying out famine relief with due care; send officials to inspect and resettle the afflicted."

sentences.zh: 洽亟奏：「使者一出，官吏必須知畏。

translations.literal: Qia urgently memorialized: "Once envoys go forth, officials are sure to know fear.
translations.idiomatic: Qia quickly memorialized in reply, "Once envoys are sent out, local officials will certainly feel the pressure to act.

sentences.zh: 其常平一司，所職何事？

translations.literal: What then is the duty of the Ever-Normal Granaries office?
translations.idiomatic: What, then, is the Ever-Normal Granaries office for?

sentences.zh: 淮、浙、江東見有使，以五使分五路，尚慮不周知。

translations.literal: On the Huai, Zhe, and Jiangdong circuits envoys are already in place; to divide five envoys among five routes still leaves concern that matters will not be fully known.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys are already active on the Huai, Zhe, and Jiangdong circuits; even splitting five envoys across five routes, you still cannot be sure every place is truly known.

sentences.zh: 今遣一人兼二三路，不過閱圖帳戶口多寡，地裡遼邈，安能遍歷乎？

translations.literal: Now to send one man to cover two or three circuits amounts only to reading registers of household counts; the territory is vast—how can he visit everywhere?
translations.idiomatic: If you send one man to cover two or three circuits, he can do no more than skim registers of household counts; the distances are vast—how could he possibly visit every affected place?

sentences.zh: 若專責常平，名正而職舉，事分而察精。」

translations.literal: If the Ever-Normal office alone is charged, the name is correct and the duty fulfilled, affairs are divided and inspection refined."
translations.idiomatic: If you charge the Ever-Normal office alone, the title fits the task, responsibilities stay clear, and oversight can be thorough."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「藝祖懲藩鎮偏重之失，不欲兵民之權聚於一夫之手。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Emperor Taizu, correcting the error of excessive weight in the military governors, did not wish military and civil authority to gather in one man's hands.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized, "Founding Emperor Taizu, learning from the excess of the military governors, did not want military and civil power concentrated in a single man's hands.

sentences.zh: 今使主兵官兼郡寄，是合兵民權為一，且屬邊徼，偏重尤甚。」

translations.literal: Now to have the commander who holds military authority also hold a prefectural commission is to unite military and civil power in one, and since it is on the frontier, the excess is especially grave."
translations.idiomatic: To let the chief military officer also hold a prefectural post is to reunite military and civil authority in one person—and on the frontier, that imbalance is all the more dangerous."

sentences.zh: 上皆嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted all of these [memorials].
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and adopted all of these proposals.

sentences.zh: 洽所論列，未嘗捃摭細故他慝以累其終身。

translations.literal: In what Qia discussed and enumerated, he never gathered petty offenses or other faults to burden a man for life.
translations.idiomatic: In his denunciations, Qia never dredged up petty faults or unrelated wrongdoing to ruin a man for life.

sentences.zh: 除右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Grandee of Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Grandee of Remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 上方銳志肄武，洽因風諫，言：「《頤》之大象：『君子以慎言語，節飲食。』

translations.literal: The emperor was then keenly devoted to military training; Qia seized the occasion to remonstrate, saying: "The Great Image of the Hexagram Yi: 'The noble man is careful in speech and temperate in food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then ardently devoted to military drill; Qia took the occasion to remonstrate, citing the Great Image of Yi: "The noble man is careful in speech and moderate in food and drink.

sentences.zh: 言語飲食猶謹節之，況其他乎？

translations.literal: If even speech and food and drink must be carefully regulated, how much more other matters?
translations.idiomatic: If even speech and eating must be regulated with care, how much more everything else?

sentences.zh: 凡筋力喘息之間，一有過差，皆非所以養其身也。」

translations.literal: In every moment of exertion and every breath, if there is the slightest excess, none of this is the way to nurture the body."
translations.idiomatic: In every exertion and every breath, the slightest excess is no way to preserve one's health."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿言無非仁義忠孝，可為萬世臣子之法，朕常念之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words are nothing but benevolence, righteousness, loyalty, and filial piety; they may serve as a model for subjects through ten thousand ages. I constantly bear them in mind."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Everything you say rests on benevolence, righteousness, loyalty, and filial piety—it could serve as a model for subjects through the ages. I keep that in mind constantly."

sentences.zh: 洽在經筵，言：「宰相代天理物，要在為國得人。

translations.literal: At the Classics Lecture, Qia said: "The chief minister stands in for Heaven in ordering all things; the essential point is to obtain men for the state.
translations.idiomatic: At the Classics Lecture, Qia said, "The chief minister stands in for Heaven in ordering the realm—the essential thing is to find the right men for the state.

sentences.zh: 人主之命相，任則勿疑。

translations.literal: When the ruler appoints a chief minister, once entrusted, do not doubt him.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler appoints a chief minister, once he is entrusted, do not doubt him.

sentences.zh: 宰相重則朝廷尊，朝廷尊則廟社安。

translations.literal: When the chief minister is weighty, the court is honored; when the court is honored, the altars of state are secure.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief minister carries real weight, the court is respected; when the court is respected, the altars of state are secure.

sentences.zh: 宰相掄才任職，當盡公心。

translations.literal: In selecting talent and assigning offices, the chief minister should exhaust impartial mind.
translations.idiomatic: In selecting talent and assigning posts, the chief minister must act with complete impartiality.

sentences.zh: 君子進則庶職舉，庶職舉則天下治。」

translations.literal: When gentlemen advance, then all offices are fulfilled; when all offices are fulfilled, then the realm is governed."
translations.idiomatic: When worthy men advance, every office is filled properly; when every office is filled properly, the realm is governed."

sentences.zh: 上首肯再三，乃曰：「卿如良金美玉，渾厚無瑕，天其以卿為朕弼耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor nodded assent again and again, then said: "You are like fine gold and beautiful jade, thick and without flaw—does Heaven mean to make you my helper?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded again and again, then said, "You are like fine gold and flawless jade—does Heaven mean to make you my right-hand minister?"

sentences.zh: 除御史中丞，奏：「薦舉請託，必競於宰執、臺諫之門，若宰執、臺諫不為人覓舉，使士大夫咸自率厲，以公道得之，豈不甚善。

translations.literal: He was appointed Censor-in-Chief and memorialized: "Recommendations and requests for favor inevitably compete at the gates of chief ministers and censors. If chief ministers and censors do not seek recommendations for others, causing all scholar-officials to discipline themselves and obtain posts through public principle, would that not be excellent?
translations.idiomatic: Appointed censor-in-chief, he memorialized, "Petitions for recommendation all converge on the doors of chief ministers and censors. If those officers stopped hunting up posts for others, scholar-officials would discipline themselves and win appointment on merit alone—would that not be far better?

sentences.zh: 或果知其人，露章以薦，亦何不可。」

translations.literal: Or if one truly knows the man, to recommend him in an open memorial—what harm in that?"
translations.idiomatic: If you truly know a man, there is nothing wrong with recommending him in an open memorial."

sentences.zh: 潭州奏強盜罪不至死應配者坐加役流，有旨具議。

translations.literal: Tanzhou reported that armed robbers whose crime did not merit death but who should be banished were instead sentenced to penal servitude with exile; an order came to deliberate fully.
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhou reported that armed robbers whose crimes did not warrant death but who should have been banished were instead sentenced to penal servitude with exile; the court ordered a full discussion.

sentences.zh: 洽曰：「強盜異他盜，以其故為也。

translations.literal: Qia said: "Armed robbery differs from other theft because it is done deliberately.
translations.idiomatic: Qia said, "Armed robbery is not ordinary theft—it is deliberate violence.

sentences.zh: 若止髡役，三年之後，圈檻一弛，豨突四出，善良受害，可勝數耶？

translations.literal: If they receive only penal servitude, after three years, once the enclosure is relaxed, they will burst forth in all directions; the good will suffer harm beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: If they receive only penal servitude, three years later, once confinement is relaxed, they will burst out everywhere—the harm to the innocent will be beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 況役時必去防閑之具，走逸結合，患尤甚焉。」

translations.literal: Moreover, during servitude the restraints must be removed; escape and banding together make the harm still worse."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, during penal servitude restraints must be loosened; escape and banding together make the danger still worse."

sentences.zh: 上深然之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 除參知政事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿每告朕用人，今卿居用人之地，不可不勉。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You have always told me about employing men; now you occupy the place of employing men—you must not fail to exert yourself."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You have always lectured me on choosing men; now you hold the post where men are chosen—you must not slacken."

sentences.zh: 上因商榷除目，洽罄謁無所顧避，上大喜曰：「五十年無此差除。」

translations.literal: When the emperor discussed appointment lists with him, Qia exhausted his recommendations without regard or avoidance; the emperor was greatly pleased and said: "In fifty years there has been no such round of appointments."
translations.idiomatic: As they discussed appointment lists, Qia recommended candidates openly, without fear or favor; the emperor was delighted and said, "In fifty years there has been no round of appointments like this."

sentences.zh: 除知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 洽累章求去，許之，除資政殿大學士、知隆興府。

translations.literal: Qia repeatedly memorialized asking to leave office; permission was granted, and he was appointed Grand Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and Prefect of Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: Qia repeatedly asked to resign; permission was granted, and he was made grand academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and prefect of Longxing.

sentences.zh: 光宗受禪，特詔言事，洽奏：「用人為萬世不易之論，臣前以此納忠壽皇，今復告于陛下。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong received the abdication, a special edict invited memorials; Qia submitted: "Employing men is a principle unchanging through ten thousand ages; I formerly offered this loyalty to Emperor Shouhuang, and now repeat it to Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong took the throne, a special edict invited memorials; Qia wrote, "Choosing the right men is a principle that never changes; I offered this counsel to Retired Emperor Xiaozong, and I offer it again to Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 屢乞歸田，尋畀提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: He repeatedly begged to return to the fields; soon he was given charge of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked to retire to his home district; soon he was given charge of the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 方未得請也，人勸之治第，洽曰：「吾書生，蒙拔擢至此，未有以報國，而先營私乎？

translations.literal: While he had not yet obtained permission [to retire], people urged him to build a mansion; Qia said: "I am a scholar; favored and raised to this point, I have not yet repaid the state—shall I first scheme for private gain?
translations.idiomatic: Before his request was granted, people urged him to build a house; Qia said, "I am only a scholar whom the court raised to high office. I have not yet repaid the state—shall I start scheming for private gain?

sentences.zh: 使吾一旦罪去，猶有先人敝廬可庇風雨，夫復何憂。」

translations.literal: Even if one day I am dismissed for crime, I still have my ancestors' worn cottage to shelter me from wind and rain—what further worry?"
translations.idiomatic: Even if I am dismissed in disgrace tomorrow, I still have my ancestors' humble cottage to shelter me from wind and rain—what more do I need?"

sentences.zh: 慶元二年致仕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingyuan he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qingyuan (1196) he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 洽常言：「居家不欺親，仕不欺君，仰不欺天，俯不欺人，幽不欺鬼神，何用求福報哉！」

translations.literal: Qia often said: "At home do not deceive kin; in office do not deceive the ruler; looking up do not deceive Heaven; looking down do not deceive men; in darkness do not deceive ghosts and spirits—what need to seek reward of blessing?"
translations.idiomatic: Qia often said, "At home, do not deceive your kin; in office, do not deceive your ruler; toward Heaven above, do not deceive; toward men below, do not deceive; in secret, do not deceive ghosts and spirits—why seek reward for virtue?"

sentences.zh: 六年七月，薨，年七十九。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year [of Qingyuan] he died; he was seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Qingyuan (1200) he died, aged seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grandee of the Golden Purple.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grandee of the Golden Purple.

sentences.zh: 洽質直端重，有大臣體，兩朝推為名臣。

translations.literal: Qia was upright in substance, dignified in bearing, possessed the bearing of a great minister, and was acclaimed as a famous minister by two reigns.
translations.idiomatic: Qia was upright and dignified, with the bearing of a great minister, and was acclaimed as a famous minister under two emperors.

sentences.zh: 有文集、奏議八十五卷。

translations.literal: He left collected writings and memorials in eighty-five juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings and memorials survive in eighty-five juan.

sentences.zh: 汪應辰

translations.literal: Wang Yingchen
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yingchen

sentences.zh: 汪應辰，字聖錫，信州玉山人。

translations.literal: Wang Yingchen, style name Shengxi, was a native of Yushan in Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yingchen, style name Shengxi, was a native of Yushan in Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼凝重異常童，五歲知讀書，屬對應聲語驚人，多識奇字。

translations.literal: As a child he was grave and unlike ordinary children; at five he could read; in matching couplets his replies came like echoes and astonished people; he knew many rare characters.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was unusually solemn; at five he could read; his impromptu couplets astonished listeners, and he knew many rare characters.

sentences.zh: 家貧無膏油，每拾薪蘇以繼晷。

translations.literal: His family was poor and had no lamp oil; he would gather firewood each day to extend the daylight [into night].
translations.idiomatic: The family was too poor for lamp oil; he gathered firewood each day to study into the night.

sentences.zh: 從人借書，一經目不忘。

translations.literal: Borrowing books from others, once he glanced at them he did not forget.
translations.idiomatic: When he borrowed books, a single reading was enough to fix them in memory.

sentences.zh: 十歲能詩，遊鄉校，郡博士戲之曰：「韓愈十三而能文，今子奚若？」

translations.literal: At ten he could compose poetry; visiting the district school, the prefectural Erudite teased him, saying: "Han Yu could write at thirteen—how do you compare?"
translations.idiomatic: At ten he could write poetry. At the district school the prefectural erudite teased him: "Han Yu could write at thirteen—how do you compare?"

sentences.zh: 應辰答曰：「仲尼三千而論道，惟公其然？」

translations.literal: Yingchen replied: "Confucius had three thousand disciples yet lectured on the Way—are you alone so?"
translations.idiomatic: Yingchen replied, "Confucius had three thousand disciples and still lectured on the Way—are you the only one who can teach?"

sentences.zh: 未冠，首貢鄉舉，試禮部，居高選。

translations.literal: Before capping age, he was first to present himself at the provincial examination; tested at the Ministry of Rites, he ranked among the top selections.
translations.idiomatic: Before he came of age, he topped the provincial examination; at the Ministry of Rites examination he ranked among the highest selections.

sentences.zh: 時趙鼎為相，延之館塾，奇之。

translations.literal: At the time Zhao Ding was chief minister; he invited him to his household school and marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ding was then chief minister; he invited Yingchen to study in his household school and was astonished by him.

sentences.zh: 紹興五年，進士第一人，年甫十八。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxing he was first among jinshi graduates; he was only eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Shaoxing (1135) he placed first among jinshi graduates, aged only eighteen.

sentences.zh: 御策以吏道、民力、兵勢為問，應辰答以為治之要，以至誠為本，在人主反求而已。

translations.literal: The imperial examination question asked about the way of officials, the strength of the people, and military power; Yingchen answered that the essential of governance is utmost sincerity, and that the ruler need only seek within himself.
translations.idiomatic: The palace examination asked about official conduct, popular strength, and military power; Yingchen answered that the key to governance is utmost sincerity, and that the ruler need only look within himself.

sentences.zh: 上覽其對，意其為老成之士，及唱第，乃年少子，引見者掖而前，上甚異之。

translations.literal: The emperor read his answer and took him for a seasoned man; when the ranks were announced, he was a young man; those presenting him supported him forward, and the emperor was greatly surprised.
translations.idiomatic: Reading his answer, the emperor took him for a seasoned man; when the ranks were announced and he proved a youth, attendants had to steady him as he was led forward, and the emperor was astonished.

sentences.zh: 鼎出班特謝。

translations.literal: Ding left the ranks to offer special thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ding stepped out of the ranks to offer special thanks.

sentences.zh: 舊進士第一人賜以御詩，及是，特書《中庸篇》以賜。

translations.literal: Formerly the first jinshi was granted an imperial poem; on this occasion, the chapter "Doctrine of the Mean" was specially written and bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the top jinshi received an imperial poem; this time the emperor personally wrote out the chapter "Doctrine of the Mean" as a gift.

sentences.zh: 初名洋，與姓字若有語病，特改賜應辰。

translations.literal: His original given name was Yang, which with his surname and style seemed to have a verbal flaw; he was specially renamed and granted Yingchen.
translations.idiomatic: His original given name was Yang, which awkwardly echoed his surname and style; the emperor specially renamed him Yingchen.

sentences.zh: 上欲即除館職，趙鼎言：「且令歷外任，養成其材。」

translations.literal: The emperor wished at once to appoint him to a Hanlin post; Zhao Ding said: "Let him first serve in outside posts and mature his talent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to appoint him at once to a Hanlin post; Zhao Ding said, "Let him serve outside the capital first and mature his talent."

sentences.zh: 乃授鎮東軍簽判。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Signing Clerk of the Zhendong Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed signing clerk of the Zhendong Army.

sentences.zh: 故事，殿試第一人無待次者，至是，取一年半闕以歸。

translations.literal: By precedent, the first place in the palace examination had no waiting period; on this occasion, a year and a half vacancy was taken before he returned.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the palace examination top graduate took office at once; this time he was given a year and a half before returning to the capital.

sentences.zh: 舍人胡寅行詞曰：「屬者延見多士，問以治道，爾年未及冠，而能推明帝王躬行之本，無曲學阿世之態。」

translations.literal: Hanlin Attendant Hu Yin drafted the credentials, saying: "Recently in audience with many scholars, the emperor asked about the way of governance; you are not yet of capping age, yet can expound the root of the emperor's personal practice, without the attitude of crooked learning and fawning on the age."
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin attendant Hu Yin drafted his appointment text: "When the emperor recently received many scholars and asked about governance, you were not yet of capping age, yet you could expound the foundation of the ruler's personal conduct, without the bent learning or flattery of the times."

sentences.zh: 應辰少受知于喻樗，既擢第，知張九成賢，問之於樗，往從之遊，所學益進。

translations.literal: Yingchen in youth received recognition from Yu Chu; after passing the examination, learning that Zhang Jiucheng was worthy, he asked Chu about him, went to study with him, and his learning advanced further.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Yingchen won the notice of Yu Chu; after passing the examination he learned that Zhang Jiucheng was a worthy man, asked Chu about him, went to study under him, and advanced further in learning.

sentences.zh: 初任，趙鼎為帥，幕府事悉諮焉。

translations.literal: In his first post, Zhao Ding was commander; all staff affairs were consulted with him.
translations.idiomatic: In his first post Zhao Ding was regional commander; every matter in the staff office was referred to Yingchen.

sentences.zh: 歲小旱，命應辰禱雨名山即應，越人語之曰：「此相公雨。」

translations.literal: In a year of slight drought, he was ordered to pray for rain on a famous mountain and rain came at once; the people of Yue called it "the chief minister's rain."
translations.idiomatic: In a year of slight drought he was sent to pray for rain on a famous mountain; rain came at once, and the people of Yue called it "the chief minister's rain."

sentences.zh: 鼎曰：「不然，乃狀元雨也。」

translations.literal: Ding said: "Not so—it is the top graduate's rain."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ding said, "No—it is the top graduate's rain."

sentences.zh: 召為秘書省正字。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Proofreader of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as proofreader of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時秦檜力主和議，王倫使還，金人欲以河南地歸我。

translations.literal: At the time Qin Hui strongly advocated peace talks; Wang Lun returned from his mission, and the Jurchens wished to return the Henan territory to us.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui was then pressing hard for peace; Wang Lun returned from his mission reporting that the Jurchens wished to return the Henan territory to Song.

sentences.zh: 應辰上疏，謂：「和議不諧非所患，和議諧矣，而因循無備之可畏。

translations.literal: Yingchen submitted a memorial, saying: "That peace talks fail to agree is not what we should fear; that peace talks succeed, yet we drift without preparation—that is fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Yingchen submitted a memorial: "Failure to reach peace is not what we should fear; success in reaching peace while we drift unprepared—that is what should terrify us.

sentences.zh: 異議不息非所患，異議息矣，而上下相蒙之可畏。

translations.literal: That dissent does not cease is not what we should fear; that dissent ceases, yet superiors and subordinates deceive one another—that is fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Unending dissent is not what we should fear; when dissent dies down and court and country deceive one another—that is what should terrify us.

sentences.zh: 金雖通和，疆場之上宜各戒嚴，以備他盜。

translations.literal: Though the Jin have opened communication for peace, on the borders each side should remain on guard to prepare against other marauders.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the Jin open peace talks, both sides should keep the borders on alert against any other threat.

sentences.zh: 今方且肆赦中外，褒寵將帥，以為休兵息民自此而始。

translations.literal: Now we are about to grant amnesty throughout the realm and reward generals, taking this as the beginning of resting arms and easing the people.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court is already granting amnesties and rewarding generals as though demobilization and peace for the people begin from this moment.

sentences.zh: 縱忘積年之恥，獨不思異時意外之患乎？

translations.literal: Even if we forget the shame of many years, do we alone not think of unforeseen calamities in future times?
translations.idiomatic: Even if we forget years of humiliation, do we not consider unforeseen disasters yet to come?

sentences.zh: 此因循無備之所以可畏也。

translations.literal: This is why drifting without preparation is fearful.
translations.idiomatic: That is why drifting unprepared is so dangerous.

sentences.zh: 方朝廷力排群議之初，大則竄逐，小則罷黜，至有一言迎合，則不次擢用。

translations.literal: When the court was first forcefully suppressing diverse opinions, the great were banished, the small dismissed; if a single word accorded [with the policy], extraordinary promotion followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the court first set out to crush dissent, major critics were banished and minor ones dismissed; a single word of compliance could win extraordinary promotion.

sentences.zh: 是以小人窺見間隙，輕躁者阿諛以希寵，畏懦者循默以備位，而忠臣正士乃無以自立於群小之間，此上下相蒙之所以可畏也。

translations.literal: Thus petty men spy out openings; the rash fawn and flatter to seek favor, the timid follow silence to keep their posts, while loyal ministers and upright men cannot stand firm among the petty—this is why mutual deception above and below is fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men therefore spy out openings: the rash fawn and flatter for favor, the timid keep silent to hold their posts, while loyal ministers and upright men cannot stand firm among the small-minded—this is why mutual deception between ruler and subjects is so dangerous.

sentences.zh: 臣願勿以和好之可無虞，而思患預防，常若敵人之至。」

translations.literal: Your subject wishes that you not take peace as free from worry, but think of calamity and guard in advance, always as if the enemy were arriving."
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty not to assume peace means safety, but to guard against disaster in advance, always as if the enemy were at the gates."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，秦檜大不悅，出通判建州，遂請祠以歸。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Qin Hui was greatly displeased; [Yingchen] was sent out as Vice Prefect of Jianzhou, then requested temple leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Qin Hui was furious; Yingchen was demoted to vice prefect of Jianzhou, then took temple leave and returned home.

sentences.zh: 寓居常山之永年院，蓬蒿滿逕，一室蕭然，饘粥不繼，人不堪其憂，處之裕如也，益以修身講學為事。

translations.literal: He lodged at the Yongnian Cloister in Changshan; wormwood filled the paths, one room was desolate, gruel did not follow gruel; others could not bear such worry, yet he dwelt at ease, devoting himself ever more to cultivating the self and lecturing on learning.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at the Yongnian Cloister in Changshan; weeds choked the paths, his single room was bare, and gruel was often lacking. Others could not have borne such poverty, but he remained at ease and devoted himself to self-cultivation and teaching.

sentences.zh: 自是凡三主管崇道觀，在隱約時，胸中浩然之氣凜然不可屈。

translations.literal: From then on he three times held charge of the Chongdao Abbey; in obscurity, the vast qi in his breast was stern and could not be bent.
translations.idiomatic: He thereafter served three terms as superintendent of the Chongdao Abbey; even in obscurity, the upright spirit in his breast could not be broken.

sentences.zh: 張九成謫邵州，交遊皆絕，應辰時通問。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiucheng was banished to Shaozhou; all his associates broke off contact, but Yingchen continued to send inquiries.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jiucheng was banished to Shaozhou, all his associates cut contact; Yingchen continued to send messages of inquiry.

sentences.zh: 及其喪父，言者猶攻之，而應辰不遠千里往吊，人皆危之。

translations.literal: When [Zhang] lost his father, critics still attacked him, yet Yingchen traveled a thousand li to offer condolences; all thought him in danger.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang's father died, critics still attacked him, yet Yingchen traveled a thousand li to mourn with him; everyone thought him in grave danger.

sentences.zh: 通判袁州，凡所予奪，人無異詞。

translations.literal: As Vice Prefect of Yuanzhou, in all he granted or withheld, people had no dissenting words.
translations.idiomatic: As vice prefect of Yuanzhou, every reward or punishment he imposed met with general approval.

sentences.zh: 始至，或以其書生易之，已乃知吏師所不能及。

translations.literal: When he first arrived, some took him for an easy mark because he was a scholar; afterward they knew even veteran administrators could not match him.
translations.idiomatic: When he first arrived, some underestimated him as a mere scholar; they soon found that even veteran administrators could not match him.

sentences.zh: 丞相趙鼎死朱崖，扶喪過郡，應辰為文祭之曰：「惟公兩登上宰，皆直艱危之時；

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhao Ding died at Zhuya; escorting the coffin through the prefecture, Yingchen composed a funerary text offering sacrifice, saying: "You alone twice ascended to chief minister, both times in dire and perilous days;
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Minister Zhao Ding died at Zhuya and his coffin passed through the prefecture, Yingchen wrote a funeral elegy: "You twice rose to chief minister, both times in dire peril;

sentences.zh: 一斥南荒，遂為死生之別。

translations.literal: One banishment to the southern wilds, and it became a parting in life and death.
translations.idiomatic: One exile to the southern wilds, and they were parted in life and death.

sentences.zh: 事已定于蓋棺，恩特容於歸骨。」

translations.literal: The matter was settled when the coffin was closed; grace especially allowed the bones to return home."
translations.idiomatic: The matter was settled at the grave; grace alone allowed his bones to return home."

sentences.zh: 吏付之火。

translations.literal: Officials handed it to the fire.
translations.idiomatic: Officials consigned it to the flames.

sentences.zh: 其子借三兵以歸，道出衢州，章傑為守，希檜意，指應辰為阿附，為死黨，符移訊鞫，偏搜行橐，求祭文不可得。

translations.literal: His son borrowed three soldiers for the journey home; passing through Qu Prefecture, Zhang Jie was prefect and, courting Qin Hui's favor, accused Yingchen of fawning attachment and being a member of a dead faction; warrants were sent to interrogate and search, ransacking his baggage, but the funerary text could not be found.
translations.idiomatic: His son borrowed three soldiers to escort the coffin home. Passing through Qu Prefecture, where Zhang Jie was prefect, Zhang—currying favor with Qin Hui—accused Yingchen of fawning on Zhao Ding and belonging to a dead faction. Warrants were issued to interrogate him and search his baggage, but the funerary text could not be found.

sentences.zh: 時胡寅遺檜書，謂此事不足竟，事乃寢。

translations.literal: At the time Hu Yin wrote to Qin Hui that this matter was not worth pursuing to the end, and the affair was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yin then wrote to Qin Hui that the matter was not worth pursuing, and the affair was dropped.

sentences.zh: 通判靜江府，逾期不得代，乃沿檄歸省其母。

translations.literal: As vice prefect of Jingjiang Prefecture, he passed his term without a replacement arriving; he therefore followed an order to return and visit his mother.
translations.idiomatic: As vice prefect of Jingjiang, he served past his term without a successor; he then followed orders to return and visit his mother.

sentences.zh: 繼差通判廣州。

translations.literal: He was next assigned as vice prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was next assigned as vice prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時檜所深忌者趙鼎、張浚，鼎既死而浚獨存，未快其意。

translations.literal: At the time those Qin Hui deeply feared were Zhao Ding and Zhang Jun; Ding was already dead but Jun alone remained, and [Qin] was not yet satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui deeply feared Zhao Ding and Zhang Jun. Ding was dead, but Jun still lived, and Qin was not yet satisfied.

sentences.zh: 江西運判張常先箋注前帥張宗元與浚詩，言於朝，其詞連逮者數十家，將誣以不軌而盡去之。

translations.literal: Jiangxi transport commissioner Zhang Changxian annotated poems exchanged between the former commander Zhang Zongyuan and Jun, reported to court, and in his wording dozens of families were implicated; they were about to charge them with sedition and remove them all.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi transport commissioner Zhang Changxian annotated poems exchanged between former commander Zhang Zongyuan and Zhang Jun and reported to court; dozens of families were implicated in a plot to charge them with sedition and purge them all.

sentences.zh: 獄既具，檜死，應辰幸而免。

translations.literal: The case was complete, but Qin died; Yingchen was fortunate and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The case was complete, but Qin Hui died; Yingchen was fortunate to escape.

sentences.zh: 明年，召為吏部郎官，遷右司。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned as Director in the Ministry of Personnel and promoted to the Right Office.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was summoned as a director in the Ministry of Personnel and promoted to the Right Office.

sentences.zh: 母老乞外，丞相苦留之曰：「方進用，未應爾。」

translations.literal: His mother was old and he begged an outside post; the chief minister pressed him to stay, saying: "You are being promoted for use—you should not do this."
translations.idiomatic: His mother was elderly and he asked for an outside post. The chief minister pressed him to stay: "You are being promoted for important work—you should not leave now."

sentences.zh: 應辰曰：「親老矣，不可緩。」

translations.literal: Yingchen said: "My parent is aged; this cannot wait."
translations.idiomatic: Yingchen said, "My mother is old; this cannot wait."

sentences.zh: 乃出知婺州。

translations.literal: He was then sent out as prefect of Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed prefect of Wu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 郡積欠上供十三萬緡，朝廷命憲漕究治，應辰謂急則擾民，乃與諸邑蠲宿逋，去苛斂，定期會，窒滲漏，悉為補發。

translations.literal: The prefecture owed 130,000 strings in arrears on tribute to the court; the court ordered the fiscal and judicial commissioners to investigate; Yingchen said haste would harass the people, so with the districts he cancelled old debts, removed harsh levies, set schedules, stopped leaks, and fully made up the payments.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture owed 130,000 strings in tribute arrears. The court ordered fiscal and judicial commissioners to investigate. Yingchen said haste would harass the people; with the districts he cancelled old debts, removed harsh levies, set schedules, stopped leaks, and fully made up the shortfall.

sentences.zh: 尋丁內艱去，廬於墓側。

translations.literal: Soon he left on mourning for his mother and built a hut beside her tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he left to mourn his mother and built a hut beside her tomb.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除秘書少監，遷權吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and promoted to Acting Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and promoted to acting minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 李顯忠冒具安豐軍功賞五千餘人，應辰奏駁之。

translations.literal: Li Xianzhong falsely claimed merit rewards for more than five thousand men at Anfeng Army; Yingchen memorialized to reject it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xianzhong falsely claimed merit rewards for more than five thousand men at Anfeng Army; Yingchen memorialized to reject the claim.

sentences.zh: 權戶部侍郎兼侍講。

translations.literal: Acting Vice Minister of Revenue and Attendant Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting vice minister of revenue and attendant lecturer.

sentences.zh: 應辰獨員當劇務，節冗費，常奏：「班直轉官三日，而堂吏增給食錢萬餘緡；

translations.literal: Yingchen alone shouldered heavy duties and cut redundant expenses, often memorializing: "When palace guards are promoted after three days, the hall clerks add more than ten thousand strings in meal money;
translations.idiomatic: Yingchen alone shouldered heavy duties and cut waste, often memorializing: "When palace guards are promoted after three days, hall clerks add more than ten thousand strings in meal money;

sentences.zh: 工匠洗澤器皿僅給百餘千，而堂吏食錢六百千；

translations.literal: when craftsmen washed ritual vessels worth only a little over a hundred strings, hall clerks took six hundred thousand in meal money;
translations.idiomatic: when craftsmen washed ritual vessels costing only a little over a hundred strings, hall clerks took six hundred thousand in meal money;

sentences.zh: 塑顯仁神御，半年功未及半，而堂吏食錢已支三萬、銀絹六百匹兩。

translations.literal: in molding the spirit image of Empress Xianren, half a year's work was not half done, yet hall clerks had already drawn thirty thousand strings in meal money and six hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: in molding the spirit image of Empress Xianren, half a year's work was less than half done, yet hall clerks had already drawn thirty thousand strings in meal money and six hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 他皆類此。」

translations.literal: Other cases were of the same kind."
translations.idiomatic: Other cases were similar."

sentences.zh: 上驚其費冗，命吏部裁之。

translations.literal: The emperor was startled at such waste and ordered the Ministry of Personnel to cut it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was startled at such waste and ordered the Ministry of Personnel to cut it.

sentences.zh: 金渝盟，詔求足食足兵之策，應辰奏曰：「陸贄有云：『將非其人，兵雖多不足恃；

translations.literal: When the Jin violated the treaty, an edict sought policies for sufficient food and troops; Yingchen memorialized: "Lu Zhi said: 'If the general is not the right man, though troops be many they cannot be relied on;
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin violated the treaty, an edict sought policies for sufficient food and troops. Yingchen memorialized: "Lu Zhi said, 'If the general is not the right man, though troops be many they cannot be relied on;

sentences.zh: 操失其柄，將雖才不為用』。

translations.literal: if one loses hold of authority, though the general have talent he will not be used.'"
translations.idiomatic: if authority is lost, though the general have talent he will not be used.'"

sentences.zh: 臣之所憂，不在兵之不足，在乎軍政之不修。

translations.literal: What your subject fears is not insufficient troops but failure to put military administration in order.
translations.idiomatic: What I fear is not insufficient troops but failure to put military administration in order.

sentences.zh: 自講和以來，將士驕惰，兵不閱習，敵未至則望風逃遁，敵既退則謾列戰功，不惟佚罰，且或受賞。

translations.literal: Since the peace talks, officers and soldiers have grown proud and lazy, troops are not drilled; before the enemy arrives they flee at the first wind, after the enemy retreats they falsely list battle achievements—not only escaping punishment but sometimes receiving rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Since the peace talks, officers and soldiers have grown proud and lazy and troops are not drilled. Before the enemy arrives they flee at the first alarm; after the enemy retreats they falsely claim battle honors—not only escaping punishment but sometimes receiving rewards.

sentences.zh: 方時無事，詔令有所不行，一旦有急，誰能聽命以赴國家之難。

translations.literal: At a time when there is no trouble, edicts are sometimes not carried out; once there is urgency, who will heed orders and rush to the state's peril?
translations.idiomatic: When all is calm, edicts sometimes go unheeded; once crisis comes, who will heed orders and rush to the state's peril?

sentences.zh: 望發英斷，賞善罰惡，使人人洗心易慮，以聽上命，然後號令必行矣。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will issue resolute judgment, reward the good and punish the evil, so that every man washes his heart and changes his thoughts to heed imperial command—then orders will surely be carried out."
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will act decisively, reward the good and punish the evil, so that every man reforms his heart to heed imperial command—then orders will surely be carried out."

sentences.zh: 三十二年建儲，以孝宗名與唐廬江王、晉楚王同，詔改為「曄」，應辰以為與唐昭宗同，白左相陳康伯，遂改今名。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year the heir apparent was established; because Xiaozong's name matched those of the Tang Prince of Lujiang and the Jin Prince of Chu, an edict changed it to "Ye"; Yingchen held that it matched Tang Zhaozong and told Left Director Chen Kangbo, and the present name was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year the heir apparent was established. Because Xiaozong's name matched the Tang Prince of Lujiang and the Jin Prince of Chu, an edict changed it to "Ye." Yingchen held that it matched Tang Zhaozong and told Left Director Chen Kangbo, and the present name was adopted.

sentences.zh: 集議秀王封爵，應辰定其稱曰「太子本生之親」。

translations.literal: When the court deliberated the enfeoffment title of the Prince of Xiu, Yingchen fixed the designation as "the crown prince's biological father."
translations.idiomatic: When the court deliberated the enfeoffment title of the Prince of Xiu, Yingchen fixed the designation as "the crown prince's biological father."

sentences.zh: 議入，內降曰：「皇太子所生父，可封秀王。」

translations.literal: When the deliberation was submitted, an inner edict said: "The crown prince's biological father may be enfeoffed as Prince of Xiu."
translations.idiomatic: When the deliberation was submitted, an inner edict said, "The crown prince's biological father may be enfeoffed as Prince of Xiu."

sentences.zh: 暨內禪，擬於傳位日降赦，應辰言：「唐太宗受禪于高祖，明年正月始改元。」

translations.literal: At the inner abdication, it was proposed to grant amnesty on the day of transfer; Yingchen said: "When Tang Taizong received the abdication from Gaozu, he changed the reign title only in the first month of the following year."
translations.idiomatic: At the inner abdication it was proposed to grant amnesty on the transfer day. Yingchen said, "When Tang Taizong received the abdication from Gaozu, he changed the reign title only in the first month of the following year."

sentences.zh: 乃從其說。

translations.literal: The court followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: The court followed his view.

sentences.zh: 又議改元「重熙」，應辰謂契丹嘗以紀年，遂改隆興。

translations.literal: They also deliberated changing the reign title to "Chongxi"; Yingchen said the Khitans had once used it as an era name, so it was changed to Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: They also deliberated changing the reign title to "Chongxi"; Yingchen said the Khitans had once used it as an era name, so it was changed to Longxing.

sentences.zh: 一朝大典禮，多應辰所定。

translations.literal: Many great court rituals of the dynasty were fixed by Yingchen.
translations.idiomatic: Many great court rituals of the dynasty were fixed by Yingchen.

sentences.zh: 議太上尊號，李燾、陳康伯密議以「光堯壽聖」為稱。

translations.literal: When deliberating the retired emperor's honorific title, Li Tao and Chen Kangbo secretly agreed on "Guangyao Shousheng" as the designation.
translations.idiomatic: When deliberating the retired emperor's honorific title, Li Tao and Chen Kangbo secretly agreed on "Guangyao Shousheng" as the designation.

sentences.zh: 及集議，或謂：「尊號始自開元，罷于元豐，今不當復，況太上視天下如棄敝屣，豈復顧此？」

translations.literal: At the collective deliberation, some said: "Honorific titles began in the Kaiyuan era and ended in the Yuanfeng era; they should not be revived now; moreover the retired emperor regards the realm as cast-off sandals—would he care for this?"
translations.idiomatic: At the collective deliberation some said, "Honorific titles began in Kaiyuan and ended in Yuanfeng; they should not be revived now. Moreover the retired emperor regards the realm as cast-off sandals—would he care for this?"

sentences.zh: 應辰主之尤力。

translations.literal: Yingchen supported this view most strongly.
translations.idiomatic: Yingchen supported this view most strongly.

sentences.zh: 或又言：「主上奉親，烏得援元豐自卻為比？」

translations.literal: Others also said: "The emperor serves his parent—how can he cite Yuanfeng to shrink back?"
translations.idiomatic: Others also said, "The emperor serves his parent—how can he cite Yuanfeng to shrink back?"

sentences.zh: 於是議狀書者半，不書者半。

translations.literal: Thus half the deliberation record supported writing the title and half opposed it.
translations.idiomatic: Thus half the deliberation record supported writing the title and half opposed it.

sentences.zh: 明日，應辰復與金安節等十二人各陳所見，大概謂「光堯」近乎「神堯」，「壽聖」乃英宗誕節，嘗以名寺。

translations.literal: The next day Yingchen again joined Jin Anjie and twelve others in stating their views, broadly holding that "Guangyao" was close to "Shenyao" and "Shousheng" was Emperor Yingzong's birthday name and had once named a temple.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yingchen again joined Jin Anjie and twelve others in stating their views, broadly holding that "Guangyao" was close to "Shenyao" and "Shousheng" was Emperor Yingzong's birthday name and had once named a temple.

sentences.zh: 御史周必大亦以為問，應辰答以「堯」豈可「光」。

translations.literal: Censor Zhou Bida also questioned this; Yingchen answered that "Yao" could not be "guanged."
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhou Bida also questioned this; Yingchen answered that Yao could not be "illuminated."

sentences.zh: 是語有聞之德壽者，高宗因上過宮，云：「汪應辰素不樂吾。」

translations.literal: This remark reached the retired emperor at Deshou Palace; Gaozong, when the emperor visited the palace, said: "Wang Yingchen has never been pleased with me."
translations.idiomatic: This remark reached Gaozong at Deshou Palace. When the emperor visited the palace, Gaozong said, "Wang Yingchen has never been pleased with me."

sentences.zh: 於是有詔：「尊號之議，已嘗奏知，不容但已。」

translations.literal: Thereupon came an edict: "The honorific deliberation has already been reported; it cannot simply be dropped."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon came an edict: "The honorific deliberation has already been reported; it cannot simply be dropped."

sentences.zh: 安節等遂奉詔。

translations.literal: Anjie and the others then followed the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Anjie and the others then followed the edict.

sentences.zh: 應辰連乞補外，遂知福州。

translations.literal: Yingchen repeatedly begged to fill an outside post and was made prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yingchen repeatedly begged for an outside post and was made prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，升敷文閣待制，舉朱熹自代。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Hanlin Attendant Drafting and recommended Zhu Xi to succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Hanlin attendant drafting and recommended Zhu Xi to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 在鎮二年，會朝廷謀蜀帥，乃以敷文閣直學士為四川制置使、知成都府。

translations.literal: After two years in the post, when the court was planning a Sichuan commander, he was made Direct Academician of the Hall for Spreading Culture and Sichuan Military Commissioner and Prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: After two years in the post, when the court was planning a Sichuan commander, he was made direct academician of the Hall for Spreading Culture, Sichuan military commissioner, and prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，特降詔撫諭。

translations.literal: On taking leave of the throne, a special edict was issued to comfort and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: On taking leave of the throne, a special edict was issued to comfort and instruct him.

sentences.zh: 入境，以書與宣撫使吳璘，令以撫諭詔申嚴號令。

translations.literal: On entering the territory, he wrote to Pacification Commissioner Wu Lin, ordering him to proclaim the comforting edict and strictly enforce commands.
translations.idiomatic: On entering the territory, he wrote to pacification commissioner Wu Lin, ordering him to proclaim the comforting edict and strictly enforce commands.

sentences.zh: 既至，免利路民餉運，徙沿邊戍兵就糧內郡，縱保勝義士復業，存左藏所解白契二百萬以備不虞，悉奏行之。

translations.literal: Once there, he exempted the people of Li Circuit from transport levies, moved border garrison troops to draw grain from inner commanderies, allowed victorious volunteers to resume their occupations, retained two million in white contracts held in the Left Treasury as a reserve, and memorialized all for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Once there, he exempted the people of Li Circuit from transport levies, moved border garrison troops to draw grain from inner commanderies, allowed victorious volunteers to resume their occupations, retained two million in white contracts held in the Left Treasury as a reserve, and memorialized all for implementation.

sentences.zh: 有謂蜀中綱馬驛程由梁、洋、金、房，山路峻險，宜浮江而下，詔吳璘措置。

translations.literal: Some said that in Sichuan the relay stages for tribute horses ran through Liang, Yang, Jin, and Fang by mountain roads steep and dangerous, and that it would be better to go by river; an edict ordered Wu Lin to arrange it.
translations.idiomatic: Some said that in Sichuan the relay stages for tribute horses ran through Liang, Yang, Jin, and Fang by steep mountain roads, and that it would be better to go by river; an edict ordered Wu Lin to arrange it.

sentences.zh: 執政、大將皆主其說，應辰與夔帥王十朋力言其不便，遂得中止。

translations.literal: Chief ministers and great generals all favored the plan; Yingchen and Kuizhou commander Wang Shipeng strongly argued against its inconvenience, and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers and great generals all favored the plan; Yingchen and Kuizhou commander Wang Shipeng strongly argued against its inconvenience, and it was stopped.

sentences.zh: 二稅勘合，每貫取二十錢，乾道詔旨嘗減三之一，有欲增之者，應辰與兩漕臣列奏，言：「勘合不以鈔計，而以貫石匹兩計，是陽為減而陰實增之也。

translations.literal: For the two-tax verification, twenty cash per string was taken; in the Qiandao era an edict had reduced it by one third; some wished to increase it; Yingchen and the two transport commissioners jointly memorialized: "Verification is not counted by notes but by strings, piculs, bolts, and taels—this is to reduce in name while actually increasing.
translations.idiomatic: For the two-tax verification, twenty cash per string was taken; in the Qiandao era an edict had reduced it by one third; some wished to increase it. Yingchen and the two transport commissioners jointly memorialized: "Verification is not counted by notes but by strings, piculs, bolts, and taels—this reduces in name while actually increasing.

sentences.zh: 以成都一路計之，歲入三十萬，今以所增為六十萬，計以四路，不知幾倍。

translations.literal: For the Chengdu circuit alone, annual intake was three hundred thousand; now the increase would make it six hundred thousand; calculated for four circuits, who knows how many times over.
translations.idiomatic: For the Chengdu circuit alone, annual intake was three hundred thousand; now the increase would make it six hundred thousand; calculated for four circuits, the multiple is unknown.

sentences.zh: 雖非興利者所便，而民受其賜多矣。」

translations.literal: Though this is not what profit-seekers favor, the people receive the benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Though profit-seekers may not like it, the people receive the greater benefit."

sentences.zh: 璘時駐蜀口武興，精兵為天下冠，既老且病，應辰密奏以關陝大將係國安危，所當預圖。

translations.literal: Lin was then stationed at Wuxing in the Shu mouth; his elite troops were the finest in the realm; he was old and ill; Yingchen secretly memorialized that the great generals of Guan and Shaan were tied to the state's safety and ought to be planned for in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was then stationed at Wuxing in the Shu mouth; his elite troops were the finest in the realm; he was old and ill. Yingchen secretly memorialized that the great generals of Guan and Shaan were tied to the state's safety and ought to be planned for in advance.

sentences.zh: 於是執政傳旨，若璘不起，令制司暫領其任。

translations.literal: Thereupon the chief ministers transmitted the instruction that if Lin could not rise, the commissioner should temporarily take his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the chief ministers transmitted the instruction that if Lin could not rise, the commissioner should temporarily take his duties.

sentences.zh: 暨璘死，應辰遂攝宣撫之職，蜀道晏然。

translations.literal: When Lin died, Yingchen then acted as pacification commissioner; the Shu road was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin died, Yingchen then acted as pacification commissioner; the Shu road was tranquil.

sentences.zh: 虞允文尋以知樞密院事宣撫四川，應辰援張浚例，乞罷制司，不許。

translations.literal: Yu Yunwen soon became Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner and pacification commissioner for Sichuan; Yingchen cited Zhang Jun's precedent and begged to abolish the commissioner's office; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen soon became bureau of military affairs commissioner and pacification commissioner for Sichuan; Yingchen cited Zhang Jun's precedent and begged to abolish the commissioner's office; permission was not granted.

sentences.zh: 總所牒委官覈四川匿契稅，應辰奏：「其不便者四，曰妨農廢業，曰縱吏擾民，曰違法害教，曰長姦起訟。

translations.literal: The general office sent orders to appoint officials to verify concealed contract taxes in Sichuan; Yingchen memorialized: "There are four inconveniences: it hinders farming and ruins livelihoods; it lets clerks harass the people; it violates law and harms instruction; it breeds wickedness and stirs litigation.
translations.idiomatic: The general office sent orders to appoint officials to verify concealed contract taxes in Sichuan. Yingchen memorialized: "There are four harms: it hinders farming and ruins livelihoods; it lets clerks harass the people; it violates law and harms instruction; it breeds wickedness and stirs litigation.

sentences.zh: 比戶部已令人自首，州縣收併已不少，其未盡者，有見行法令，不宜為此煩擾。」

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue has already ordered people to confess; prefectures and districts have collected no small amount; for what remains there are existing statutes—it is not fitting to harass people further."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue has already ordered people to confess; prefectures and districts have collected no small amount; for what remains there are existing statutes—it is not fitting to harass people further."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「論極有理，速罷止之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The argument is extremely reasonable; stop it quickly."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The argument is extremely reasonable; stop it quickly."

sentences.zh: 蜀大旱，詔問救荒之策，應辰奏：「利、閬、綿、梓軍馬糧料，隨民力均敷，官雖支糴錢，民不得半價，若選官就歲熟處糴之，可以寬民力，第無錢束手，乞給度牒。」

translations.literal: Sichuan suffered great drought; an edict asked policies for famine relief; Yingchen memorialized: "In Li, Lang, Mian, and Zi, military horse grain rations are spread according to the people's strength; though the government pays grain money, the people receive less than half price; if officials are chosen to buy grain where the harvest is good, popular strength can be eased—but there is no money and hands are tied; I beg issuance of quota certificates."
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan suffered great drought; an edict asked policies for famine relief. Yingchen memorialized: "In Li, Lang, Mian, and Zi, military horse grain rations are spread according to the people's strength; though the government pays grain money, the people receive less than half price. If officials are chosen to buy grain where the harvest is good, popular strength can be eased—but there is no money; I beg issuance of quota certificates."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「汪應辰治蜀甚有聲，且留意民事如此。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Wang Yingchen governs Shu with great reputation and attends to the people's affairs thus."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Wang Yingchen governs Shu with great reputation and attends to the people's affairs thus."

sentences.zh: 給度牒四百，永為糴本振濟，遂移書諸路漕臣，亟救荒，且以綿、劍和糴告之，而全蜀蒙惠。

translations.literal: Four hundred quota certificates were granted, permanently as capital for grain purchase and relief; he then wrote to transport commissioners of various circuits to relieve famine urgently, and informed them of grain purchase in Mian and Jian; all Shu benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Four hundred quota certificates were granted, permanently as capital for grain purchase and relief; he then wrote to transport commissioners of various circuits to relieve famine urgently, and informed them of grain purchase in Mian and Jian; all Shu benefited.

sentences.zh: 劉珙拜同知樞密院事，進言曰：「汪應辰、陳良翰、張栻學行才能，臣所不及。」

translations.literal: Liu Gong was made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and advanced, saying: "Wang Yingchen, Chen Lianghan, and Zhang Shi in learning, conduct, and ability surpass your subject."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gong was made vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and advanced, saying, "Wang Yingchen, Chen Lianghan, and Zhang Shi in learning, conduct, and ability surpass your subject."

sentences.zh: 已，得旨召還。

translations.literal: Before long he received an edict to return.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he received an edict to return.

sentences.zh: 邛之安仁年饑，挻起為盜，害及旁郡，即具奏，且檄茶馬使招捕。

translations.literal: In Anren of Qiong, famine in one year stirred people to become bandits, harming neighboring commanderies; he immediately memorialized and also ordered the tea-and-horse commissioner to recruit and capture them.
translations.idiomatic: In Anren of Qiong, famine in one year stirred people to become bandits, harming neighboring commanderies; he immediately memorialized and also ordered the tea-and-horse commissioner to recruit and capture them.

sentences.zh: 旬月間，誅其渠魁，餘悉撫定。

translations.literal: Within a month the ringleaders were executed and the rest were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month the ringleaders were executed and the rest were pacified.

sentences.zh: 或白之虞允文曰：「汪帥得無掩盜事不上聞乎？」

translations.literal: Someone told Yu Yunwen: "Does Commander Wang perhaps conceal the bandit affair and not report upward?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Yu Yunwen, "Does Commander Wang perhaps conceal the bandit affair and not report upward?"

sentences.zh: 宣司乃密奏，使人紿應辰曰：「邛寇事未敢奏，不審制司如何？」

translations.literal: The pacification office then secretly memorialized and sent a man to deceive Yingchen, saying: "The Qiong bandit affair has not yet been daringly reported—how does the commissioner's office view it?"
translations.idiomatic: The pacification office then secretly memorialized and sent a man to deceive Yingchen, saying, "The Qiong bandit affair has not yet been daringly reported—how does the commissioner's office view it?"

sentences.zh: 應辰以奏檢報之，允文內愧。

translations.literal: Yingchen reported with his memorial copy; Yunwen felt ashamed within.
translations.idiomatic: Yingchen reported with his memorial copy; Yunwen felt ashamed within.

sentences.zh: 將行，代納成都一府激賞絹估三萬三千九百八十四匹。

translations.literal: When about to depart, he paid on behalf of the Chengdu prefecture 33,984 bolts of appraisal silk for merit rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When about to depart, he paid on behalf of the Chengdu prefecture 33,984 bolts of appraisal silk for merit rewards.

sentences.zh: 冬，入覲，陛對，以畏天愛民為言。

translations.literal: In winter he entered audience; at the throne he spoke of revering Heaven and loving the people.
translations.idiomatic: In winter he entered audience; at the throne he spoke of revering Heaven and loving the people.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿久在蜀，寬朕西顧憂，軍政民事革弊殆盡，蜀中除虛額，民間當被實惠。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You were long in Shu and eased my western worries; in military and civil affairs you reformed abuses nearly to the end; in Shu false quotas were removed and the people should receive real benefit."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You were long in Shu and eased my western worries; in military and civil affairs you reformed abuses nearly to the end; in Shu false quotas were removed and the people should receive real benefit."

sentences.zh: 應辰奏：「虛額去則州縣寬，尚有兩事，曰預借，曰對糴。

translations.literal: Yingchen memorialized: "When false quotas are removed, prefectures and districts are eased; yet two matters remain: advance collection and paired grain purchase.
translations.idiomatic: Yingchen memorialized, "When false quotas are removed, prefectures and districts are eased; yet two matters remain: advance collection and paired grain purchase.

sentences.zh: 預借乃州縣累歲相仍，對糴則以補州縣闕乏，民輸米一石，即就糴一石，或半價，或不支，且多取贏。

translations.literal: Advance collection is what prefectures and districts have carried on for years; paired purchase supplements prefectural and district shortfalls—the people deliver one picul of rice and the government purchases one picul at once, or at half price, or pays nothing, and often takes surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Advance collection is what prefectures and districts have carried on for years; paired purchase supplements prefectural and district shortfalls—the people deliver one picul of rice and the government purchases one picul at once, or at half price, or pays nothing, and often takes surplus.

sentences.zh: 陛下近捐百萬除預借之弊，對糴患止數州，願並除之，則弊革無餘矣。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty recently gave up a million to remove the abuse of advance collection; the harm of paired purchase affects only a few prefectures—I hope both may be removed, then abuses will be reformed without remainder."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty recently gave up a million to remove the abuse of advance collection; the harm of paired purchase affects only a few prefectures—I hope both may be removed, then abuses will be reformed without remainder."

sentences.zh: 除吏部尚書，尋兼翰林學士並侍讀。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Personnel and soon also Hanlin Academician and Attendant Reader.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed minister of personnel and soon also Hanlin academician and attendant reader.

sentences.zh: 論愛民六事，廟堂議不合，不悅者眾。

translations.literal: He discussed six matters of loving the people; the court deliberated and disagreed; many were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: He discussed six matters of loving the people; the court deliberated and disagreed; many were displeased.

sentences.zh: 一日，陳良祐登對，上告以「汪應辰言卿在蜀多誕謾。」

translations.literal: One day Chen Liangyou appeared for audience; the emperor told him: "Wang Yingchen says you told many lies in Shu."
translations.idiomatic: One day Chen Liangyou appeared for audience; the emperor told him, "Wang Yingchen says you told many lies in Shu."

sentences.zh: 良祐奏：「臣與應辰昨同從班，應辰請外，得衢州，臣惜其去，同奏留之。

translations.literal: Liangyou memorialized: "Your subject and Yingchen were formerly colleagues in the same rank; Yingchen asked for an outside post and received Qu Prefecture; your subject regretted his leaving and jointly memorialized to keep him.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyou memorialized, "Your subject and Yingchen were formerly colleagues in the same rank; Yingchen asked for an outside post and received Qu Prefecture; your subject regretted his leaving and jointly memorialized to keep him.

sentences.zh: 時邊奏方急，臣不知應辰將為便私計也。

translations.literal: Border reports were then urgent; your subject did not know Yingchen was planning private convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Border reports were then urgent; your subject did not know Yingchen was planning private convenience.

sentences.zh: 奏既上，應辰以此大憾，乃為是說以中臣耳。」

translations.literal: Once the memorial was submitted, Yingchen greatly resented this and made this charge to strike at your subject."
translations.idiomatic: Once the memorial was submitted, Yingchen greatly resented this and made this charge to strike at your subject."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「乃爾邪！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "So it is!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "So it is!"

sentences.zh: 應辰在朝多革弊事，中貴人皆側目。

translations.literal: Yingchen in court reformed many abuses; the powerful eunuchs all glared sidelong.
translations.idiomatic: Yingchen in court reformed many abuses; the powerful eunuchs all glared sidelong.

sentences.zh: 德壽宮方甃石池，以水銀浮金鳧魚於上，上過之，高宗指示曰：「水銀正乏，此買之汪尚書家。」

translations.literal: At Deshou Palace they were paving a stone pool and floated golden ducks and fish on mercury; when the emperor passed, Gaozong pointed and said: "Mercury is scarce; this was bought from Minister Wang's house."
translations.idiomatic: At Deshou Palace they were paving a stone pool and floated golden ducks and fish on mercury; when the emperor passed, Gaozong pointed and said, "Mercury is scarce; this was bought from Minister Wang's house."

sentences.zh: 上怒曰：「汪應辰力言朕置房廓與民爭利，乃自販水銀邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said: "Wang Yingchen strongly urged that I set up shops to compete with the people for profit—yet he himself sells mercury?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor angrily said, "Wang Yingchen strongly urged that I set up shops to compete with the people for profit—yet he himself sells mercury?"

sentences.zh: 應辰知之，力求去。

translations.literal: When Yingchen learned of it, he urgently sought to leave.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingchen learned of it, he urgently sought to leave.

sentences.zh: 會復出發運均輸之旨，歎曰：「吾不可留矣，但力辨群枉，則補外之請自得。」

translations.literal: When the order to revive transport and equalization was issued again, he sighed: "I cannot remain; but if I forcefully refute the crowd's wrong, my request for an outside post will come of itself."
translations.idiomatic: When the order to revive transport and equalization was issued again, he sighed, "I cannot remain; but if I forcefully refute the crowd's wrong, my request for an outside post will come of itself."

sentences.zh: 乃力論其事有害無利，遂以端明殿學士知平江府。

translations.literal: He then strongly argued that the matter harmed without benefiting, and was made Academician of the Hall for Brightening Governance and Prefect of Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He then strongly argued that the matter harmed without benefiting, and was made academician of the Hall for Brightening Governance and prefect of Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 韓玉被旨揀馬，過郡，應辰簡其禮。

translations.literal: Han Yu received an order to select horses and passed through the prefecture; Yingchen simplified his reception.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu received an order to select horses and passed through the prefecture; Yingchen simplified his reception.

sentences.zh: 玉歸，譖之於上曰：「臣所過州縣，未有若平江之不治者。」

translations.literal: Yu returned and slandered him to the emperor: "Of all prefectures and districts your subject passed through, none was as poorly governed as Pingjiang."
translations.idiomatic: Yu returned and slandered him to the emperor: "Of all prefectures and districts your subject passed through, none was as poorly governed as Pingjiang."

sentences.zh: 上怪之。

translations.literal: The emperor found it strange.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found it strange.

sentences.zh: 平江米綱至，有折閱，事上，連貶秩。

translations.literal: When Pingjiang's grain transport arrived, there was shortage in delivery; the matter was reported upward and his rank was reduced in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Pingjiang's grain transport arrived, there was shortage in delivery; the matter was reported upward and his rank was reduced in succession.

sentences.zh: 力疾請祠，自是臥家不起矣，以淳熙三年二月卒於家。

translations.literal: Ill, he urgently begged temple leave; from then he lay at home unable to rise, and in the second month of the third year of Chunxi died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Ill, he urgently begged temple leave; from then he lay at home unable to rise, and in the second month of the third year of Chunxi (1176) died at home.

sentences.zh: 應辰接物溫遜，遇事特立不回，流落嶺嶠十有七年。

translations.literal: Yingchen in dealing with others was warm and modest; in affairs he stood alone and did not bend back; he wandered in the southern ranges for seventeen years.
translations.idiomatic: Yingchen in dealing with others was warm and modest; in affairs he stood alone and did not bend back; he wandered in the southern ranges for seventeen years.

sentences.zh: 檜死，始還朝，剛方正直，敢言不避。

translations.literal: When Hui died, he then returned to court; he was firm and upright, and spoke boldly without holding back.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin Hui died, he was at last able to return to court. Upright and resolute, he spoke candidly without fear or evasion.

sentences.zh: 少從呂居仁、胡安國游，張栻、呂祖謙深器許之，告以造道之方。

translations.literal: In youth he followed Lü Juren and Hu Anguo in study; Zhang Shi and Lü Zuqian deeply valued and approved of him, and told him the method of attaining the Way.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied under Lü Juren and Hu Anguo. Zhang Shi and Lü Zuqian held him in high regard and taught him how to pursue the Way.

sentences.zh: 嘗釋克己之私如用兵克敵，「《易》懲忿窒欲，《書》剛制於酒，懲窒、剛制皆克勝義，可不常省察乎？」

translations.literal: He once explained restraining private desires as using troops to conquer enemies: "The Book of Changes [says] 'restrain anger and check desires'; the Book of Documents [says] 'be firm in restraining wine.' Restraining and checking, and firm restraining, all carry the meaning of conquering and overcoming—should one not constantly examine oneself?"
translations.idiomatic: He once likened restraining selfish desires to using armies to defeat enemies: "The Book of Changes teaches us to restrain anger and check desires; the Book of Documents teaches us to be firm in restraining wine. Restraint, checking, and firm control all embody the meaning of overcoming and conquering—should we not constantly examine ourselves in this light?"

sentences.zh: 其義理之精如此。

translations.literal: Such was the refinement of his principle and reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the subtlety and precision of his moral reasoning.

sentences.zh: 好賢樂善，出於天性，尤篤友愛，嘗以先疇遜其兄衢，雖無屋可居不顧也。

translations.literal: He loved worthies and delighted in good, [which] came from his inborn nature; especially deep in friendship and love, he once yielded his ancestral fields to his elder brother Qu, and though he had no house in which to dwell, he paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Loving worthy men and delighting in good deeds came naturally to him. Deeply devoted to friendship and kinship, he once yielded his ancestral estate to his elder brother Qu, caring nothing that he himself was left without a house to live in.

sentences.zh: 子達，繼登進士第，仕至吏部尚書、端明殿學士。

translations.literal: His son Da, in succession passed the jinshi examination, and in office reached Minister of Personnel and Academician of the Hall for Brightening Governance.
translations.idiomatic: His son Da also passed the jinshi examination and rose to serve as Minister of Personnel and academician of the Hall for Brightening Governance.

sentences.zh: 王十朋

translations.literal: Wang Shipeng
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shipeng

sentences.zh: 王十朋，字龜齡，溫州樂清人。

translations.literal: Wang Shipeng, styled Guiling, was a man of Yueqing in Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shipeng, whose style name was Guiling, was a native of Yueqing in Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 資穎悟，日誦數千言。

translations.literal: Endowed with keen intelligence, he daily recited several thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: Naturally quick-witted, he could recite several thousand characters each day.

sentences.zh: 及長，有文行，聚徒梅溪，受業者以百數。

translations.literal: When grown, he possessed literary accomplishment and conduct; he gathered disciples at Meixi, and those receiving instruction numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age, he was noted for both literary talent and moral conduct. He gathered disciples at Meixi, and those who studied under him numbered in the hundreds.

sentences.zh: 入太學，主司異其文。

translations.literal: He entered the Imperial College; the chief examiner regarded his essays as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial College, where the chief examiner found his essays outstanding.
