sentences.zh: 秦檜死，上親政，策士，諭考官曰：「對策中有陳朝政切直者，並置上列。」

translations.literal: When Qin Hui died, the emperor personally administered affairs and examined candidates, instructing the examiners: "Among those answering policy questions, those who frankly discuss court affairs—place them all in the upper ranks."
translations.idiomatic: After Qin Hui died, the emperor took personal charge of government and held the policy examination. He told the examiners, "Place at the top of the list any candidate whose answers speak frankly and directly about court affairs."

sentences.zh: 十朋以「權」為對，大略曰：「攬權者，非欲衡石程書如秦皇，傳餐聽政如隋文，強明自任、不任宰相如唐德宗，精於吏事、以察為明如唐宣宗，蓋欲陛下懲既往而戒未然，威福一出於上而已。

translations.literal: Shipeng took "consolidating power" as his theme and said in general: "To consolidate power is not to weigh stones and measure books like the First Emperor of Qin, nor to pass meals forward while hearing affairs of state like Emperor Wen of Sui, nor to be forceful and bright in relying on oneself and not entrusting the chancellor like Emperor Dezong of Tang, nor to be skilled in administrative matters and take scrutiny as clarity like Emperor Xuanzong of Tang—it is simply that Your Majesty should take warning from what has passed and guard against what has not yet come, so that authority and favor issue from above alone.
translations.idiomatic: Shipeng chose "consolidating power" as his theme and argued, in essence: "Consolidating power does not mean weighing every stone and tallying every document like the First Emperor of Qin, nor passing meals forward while holding court like Emperor Wen of Sui, nor insisting on one's own judgment and refusing to rely on the chancellor like Emperor Dezong of Tang, nor treating administrative minutiae as wisdom like Emperor Xuanzong of Tang. It means that Your Majesty should learn from past mistakes, guard against future ones, and keep authority and favor in your own hands alone.

sentences.zh: 嘗有鋪翠之禁，而以翠羽為首飾者自若，是豈法令不可禁乎？

translations.literal: There was once a ban on kingfisher-feather ornamentation, yet those who used kingfisher feathers as head ornaments remained as before—is this because the law and orders cannot be enforced?
translations.idiomatic: There was once a ban on kingfisher-feather ornamentation, yet people continued to wear kingfisher feathers in their hair as before. Is this because the law cannot be enforced?

sentences.zh: 抑宮中服澣濯之化，衣不曳地之風未形於外乎？

translations.literal: Or is it rather that the palace's influence in washing and mending clothes, and the wind of not letting garments trail on the ground, has not yet appeared outwardly?
translations.idiomatic: Or is it rather that the palace's example of frugal laundering and the custom of not letting robes drag on the ground has not yet been felt outside the inner court?

sentences.zh: 法之至公者莫如選士，名器之至重者莫如科第。

translations.literal: Of laws, the most public is none other than selecting scholars; of titles and offices, the most weighty is none other than the examination ranks.
translations.idiomatic: No law is more fundamentally impartial than the selection of scholars, and no honor is weightier than the examination ranks.

sentences.zh: 往歲權臣子孫、門客類竊巍科，有司以國家名器為媚權臣之具，而欲得人可乎？

translations.literal: In past years the sons and grandsons and clients of powerful ministers mostly stole lofty examination honors; the officials took the state's titles and offices as instruments to flatter powerful ministers—yet could they expect to obtain worthy men?
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the sons, grandsons, and clients of powerful ministers have repeatedly captured top examination honors, while the officials treated the state's titles and offices as tools for currying favor with the powerful. Under such conditions, how could worthy men be found?

sentences.zh: 願陛下正身以為本，任賢以為助，博采兼聽以收其效。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to rectify your person as the foundation, employ the worthy as assistance, and broadly gather and jointly listen so as to achieve the effect."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty make personal rectitude the foundation, employ worthy men as your support, and broadly gather opinions and listen to all sides so that these reforms may succeed."

sentences.zh: 幾萬餘言。

translations.literal: It ran to nearly ten thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: The answer ran to nearly ten thousand words.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其經學淹通，議論醇正，遂擢為第一。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his thorough mastery of the classics and his pure and upright discourse, and therefore promoted him to first place.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his thorough mastery of the classics and the purity of his argument, and placed him first in the examination.

sentences.zh: 學者爭傳誦其策，以擬古晁、董。

translations.literal: Scholars competed to copy and recite his policy answer, comparing it to the ancients Chao and Dong.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars competed to copy and recite his policy answer, likening it to the work of the great Han memorialists Chao Cuo and Dong Zhongshu.

sentences.zh: 上用其言，嚴銷金鋪翠之令，取交阯所貢翠物焚之。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted his words, strictly enforced the ban on gold-inlaid kingfisher ornamentation, and took the kingfisher tribute from Jiaozhi and burned it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor acted on his advice, strictly enforced the ban on gold-inlaid kingfisher ornamentation, and had the kingfisher tribute from Jiaozhi burned.

sentences.zh: 謂「十朋乃朕親擢」。

translations.literal: He said, "Shipeng was personally promoted by me."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Shipeng was personally selected by me."

sentences.zh: 授紹興府簽判。

translations.literal: He was appointed Signing Secretary of Shaoxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed signing secretary of Shaoxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 既至，或以書生易之，十朋裁決如神，吏姦不行。

translations.literal: When he arrived, some looked down on him as a mere scholar; Shipeng rendered judgments like a spirit, and clerical corruption could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, some looked down on him as a mere scholar, but Shipeng rendered judgments with uncanny precision, and corrupt clerks could find no opening.

sentences.zh: 時以四科求士，帥王師心謂十朋身兼四者，獨以應詔。

translations.literal: At the time the court sought men by four categories; the prefect Wang Shixin considered that Shipeng personally combined all four and nominated him alone in response to the edict.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court was recruiting men under four categories of merit. Prefect Wang Shixin judged that Shipeng embodied all four and nominated him alone in response to the imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 召為秘書郎兼建王府小學教授。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Secretary of the Secretariat and concurrently Instructor of the Primary School of the Heir Apparent's Establishment.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as a secretary in the Secretariat and concurrently as instructor of the primary school in the Heir Apparent's establishment.

sentences.zh: 先是，教授入講堂居賓位，十朋不可，皇孫特加禮而位教授中坐。

translations.literal: Previously, when instructors entered the lecture hall they sat in the guest seat; Shipeng would not accept this, and the imperial grandson specially showed him honor and seated the instructor in the central seat.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when instructors entered the lecture hall they took the guest seat. Shipeng refused to accept this arrangement, and the imperial grandson specially honored him by seating the instructor in the central place.

sentences.zh: 金將渝盟，十朋輪對，言：「自建炎至今，金未嘗不內相殘賊，然一主斃，一主生，曷嘗為中國利？

translations.literal: When the Jin were about to break the alliance, Shipeng presented a rotating memorial, saying: "From the Jianyan era to the present, the Jin have never ceased killing one another internally; yet when one ruler dies, another is born—when has this ever benefited China?
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin were about to break the alliance, Shipeng presented a rotating memorial, saying, "From the Jianyan era to the present, the Jin have never ceased fighting among themselves. Yet whenever one ruler dies, another rises—when has this ever benefited the Song?

sentences.zh: 要在自備如何。

translations.literal: What matters is how we prepare ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: What matters is how well we prepare ourselves.

sentences.zh: 禦敵莫急於用人，今有天資忠義、材兼文武可為將相者，有長於用兵、士卒樂為之用可為大帥者，或投閒置散，或老於藩郡，願起而用之，以寢敵謀，以圖恢復。」

translations.literal: In repelling the enemy nothing is more urgent than employing men. Now there are those endowed by nature with loyalty and righteousness and talents combining civil and military who can serve as generals and chancellors; there are those skilled in using troops whose soldiers delight to serve under them and who can serve as great commanders—some are cast aside in idleness, some grow old in border prefectures. I wish that they be raised and employed to put the enemy's schemes to rest and to plan recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing is more urgent in repelling the enemy than putting the right men in office. There are men of natural loyalty and righteousness whose talents unite civil and military ability and who could serve as generals and chancellors; there are men skilled in command whose soldiers gladly follow them and who could serve as great marshals. Some lie idle in obscurity, others grow old in distant prefectures. I ask that they be summoned and employed to frustrate the enemy's designs and advance the cause of recovery."

sentences.zh: 蓋指張浚、劉錡也。

translations.literal: This referred to Zhang Jun and Liu Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He was referring to Zhang Jun and Liu Qi.

sentences.zh: 又言：「今權雖歸於陛下，政復出於多門，是一檜死百檜生也。

translations.literal: He also said: "Today although power has returned to Your Majesty, government again issues from many gates—this is one Hui dead and a hundred Hui born.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Although power has now returned to Your Majesty, government again flows from many doors—one Hui is dead, but a hundred Huies are being born.

sentences.zh: 楊存中以三衙而交結北司，以盜大權。

translations.literal: Yang Cunzhong, holding the three palace guard commands, formed ties with the Northern Bureau and thereby usurped great power.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Cunzhong, commanding the three palace guard armies, cultivated ties with the Northern Bureau and thereby usurped great power.

sentences.zh: 漢之禍起於恭、顯，王氏之相為終始；

translations.literal: Han's calamity arose from Hong and Xian; the Wang clan's chancellorship ran from beginning to end;
translations.idiomatic: Han dynastic disaster began with the eunuchs Hong and Xian; the Wang clan's hold on the chancellorship ran from beginning to end;

sentences.zh: 唐之禍起於北軍，藩鎮之相為表裏。

translations.literal: Tang's calamity arose from the Northern Armies; the military governors acted as outer and inner [supports to one another].
translations.idiomatic: Tang dynastic disaster began with the Northern Armies; the military governors acted as outer and inner supports to one another.

sentences.zh: 今以管軍位三公，利源皆入其門，陰結諸將，相為黨援。

translations.literal: Now one who commands armies holds the rank of Three Excellencies, and sources of profit all enter his gate; he secretly joins with various generals and acts as mutual partisan support.
translations.idiomatic: Today the commander of the palace armies holds rank among the Three Excellencies, every lucrative post flows through his household, and he secretly binds the generals together in mutual partisan support.

sentences.zh: 樞密本兵之地，立班甘居其後。

translations.literal: The Bureau of Military Affairs is the original seat of military authority, yet in court order it stands willingly behind.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs is the original seat of military authority, yet in court order it is made to stand behind him.

sentences.zh: 子弟親戚，佈滿清要。

translations.literal: Sons, younger brothers, and relatives by marriage fill the important and pure offices.
translations.idiomatic: His sons, younger brothers, and in-laws fill every prestigious office.

sentences.zh: 臺諫論列，委曲庇護，風憲獨不行于管軍之門，何以為國！

translations.literal: Censors and remonstrators who spoke out were tactfully shielded; the wind of impeachment alone did not reach the gate of the army commander—how can this be called governing a state!
translations.idiomatic: When censors and remonstrators spoke out, they were tactfully shielded; the power of impeachment did not reach the army commander's door. How can a state be governed this way?

sentences.zh: 至若清資加於噲五；

translations.literal: As for pure offices being added to Kuai Wu;
translations.idiomatic: Pure offices have been lavished on men like Kuai Wu;

sentences.zh: 高爵濫於醫門；

translations.literal: high ranks have been wantonly granted at the physician's gate;
translations.idiomatic: high ranks have been wantonly handed out at a physician's door;

sentences.zh: 諸軍承受，威福自恣，甚于唐之監軍；

translations.literal: the army receivers exercised authority and favor at will, worse than Tang dynasty army supervisors;
translations.idiomatic: army receivers have wielded authority and favor as they pleased, worse than the Tang dynasty army supervisors;

sentences.zh: 皇城邏卒，旁午察事，甚于周之監謗；

translations.literal: Imperial city patrol soldiers crisscrossed in investigating affairs, worse than Zhou dynasty slander supervisors;
translations.idiomatic: imperial city patrol soldiers have crisscrossed the capital gathering intelligence, worse than the Zhou dynasty slander supervisors;

sentences.zh: 將帥剝下賂上，結怨三軍；

translations.literal: generals stripped those below to bribe those above, creating resentment throughout the three armies;
translations.idiomatic: generals have stripped their subordinates to bribe their superiors, breeding resentment throughout the armies;

sentences.zh: 道路捕人為卒，結怨百姓；

translations.literal: on the roads men were seized as soldiers, creating resentment among the common people;
translations.idiomatic: on the roads men have been seized and pressed into service, breeding resentment among the people;

sentences.zh: 皆非治世事。」

translations.literal: none of these are ways to govern the age."
translations.idiomatic: none of these are ways to govern an empire."

sentences.zh: 上嘉納，戢邏卒，罷諸軍承受，更定樞密、管軍班次，解楊存中兵權，其言大略施行。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted [his words], restrained the patrol soldiers, abolished the army receivers, revised the court order of the Bureau of Military Affairs and the army commander, removed Yang Cunzhong's military authority, and largely implemented his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted his advice, restrained the patrol soldiers, abolished the army receivers, revised the court precedence of the Bureau of Military Affairs and the army commander, stripped Yang Cunzhong of military authority, and largely put his proposals into effect.

sentences.zh: 秦檜久塞言路，至是十朋與馮方、胡憲、查籥、李浩相繼論事，太學生為《五賢詩》述其事。

translations.literal: Qin Hui had long blocked the path of speech; at this time Shipeng, together with Feng Fang, Hu Xian, Zha Yao, and Li Hao, successively discussed affairs, and students of the Imperial College composed the "Poem of the Five Worthies" to recount the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui had long blocked free speech. Now Shipeng, together with Feng Fang, Hu Xian, Zha Yao, and Li Hao, spoke out in succession on state affairs, and Imperial College students composed the "Poem of the Five Worthies" to commemorate what they had done.

sentences.zh: 除著作郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Drafting Officer.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed drafting officer.

sentences.zh: 三十一年正月，風雷雨雪交作，十朋以為陽不勝陰之驗，遣陳康伯書，冀以《春秋》災異之說力陳於上，崇陽抑陰，以弭天變。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirty-first year, wind, thunder, rain, and snow occurred together; Shipeng took this as a sign that yang did not overcome yin, and sent a letter to Chen Kangbo, hoping that through the Spring and Autumn theory of calamities and anomalies he might forcefully present the matter to the emperor, exalt yang and suppress yin, and thereby quell the heavenly change.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirty-first year, wind, thunder, rain, and snow struck together. Shipeng took this as a sign that yin was overpowering yang and wrote to Chen Kangbo, hoping that through the Spring and Autumn doctrine of calamities and portents he might forcefully lay the matter before the emperor, exalt yang and suppress yin, and thereby appease Heaven's warning.

sentences.zh: 遷大宗正丞，亟請祠歸。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court and urgently requested temple leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of the Imperial Clan Court and urgently requested leave for temple service so he could return home.

sentences.zh: 金犯邊，起劉錡為江、淮、浙西制置，張浚帥金陵，悉如其言。

translations.literal: When the Jin violated the border, Liu Qi was raised as Pacification Commissioner of the Jiang, Huai, and Western Zhe circuits, and Zhang Jun commanded Jinling—all exactly as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin violated the border, Liu Qi was summoned as pacification commissioner of the Jiang, Huai, and Western Zhe circuits, and Zhang Jun was placed in command at Jinling—just as Shipeng had urged.

sentences.zh: 孝宗受禪，起知嚴州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong received the abdication, Shipeng was summoned to serve as prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong ascended the throne, Shipeng was summoned to serve as prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 召對，首言：「太皇非倦勤時，而以大器付陛下，賢于堯、舜，陛下當思以副太上者。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, he first said: "The Retired Emperor did not abdicate from weariness of labor, yet entrusted the great vessel to Your Majesty—more worthy than Yao and Shun. Your Majesty should think how to live up to the Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned for audience, he began by saying, "The Retired Emperor did not abdicate from weariness of rule, yet entrusted the empire to Your Majesty—a deed more generous than Yao or Shun. Your Majesty should consider how to live up to that trust.

sentences.zh: 今社稷之安危，生民之休戚，人才之進退，朝廷之刑賞，宜若舜之協堯，斷然行之，以盡繼述之道。」

translations.literal: Now the safety or danger of the altars of state, the weal or woe of the people, the advancement or withdrawal of talent, and the punishments and rewards of the court should be like Shun's assisting Yao—decisively carried out—to fulfill the way of succession and continuation."
translations.idiomatic: The safety of the altars of state, the welfare of the people, the advancement of talent, and the punishments and rewards of the court should all be handled as Shun assisted Yao—decisively and without hesitation—to fulfill the duty of succession."

sentences.zh: 拜司封郎中，累遷國子司業。

translations.literal: He was appointed Lang of the Department of Population and successively promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed lang of the Department of Population and was successively promoted to vice director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 言：「今居位者往往職之不舉，宜有以革之。

translations.literal: He said: "Those now in office often fail to perform their duties; there should be some means to reform this.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Those now in office often fail to perform their duties; there should be some way to reform this.

sentences.zh: 人主有大職三，任賢、納諫、賞罰是也。」

translations.literal: The ruler has three great duties: employing the worthy, accepting remonstrance, and [administering] rewards and punishments."
translations.idiomatic: A ruler has three great duties: employing worthy men, accepting remonstrance, and administering rewards and punishments."

sentences.zh: 上嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised this.

sentences.zh: 除起居舍人，升侍講。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant of the Diaries of Activity and Presence and promoted to Court Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed attendant of the diaries of activity and presence and promoted to court lecturer.

sentences.zh: 時左右史失職久，十朋除起居郎，胡銓奏四事，語在《胡銓傳》。

translations.literal: At the time the Left and Right Historiographers had long been derelict in duty; when Shipeng was appointed Attendant of the Diaries of Activity and Presence, Hu Quan memorialized on four matters—the account is in the "Biography of Hu Quan."
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Historiographers had long neglected their duties. When Shipeng was appointed attendant of the diaries of activity and presence, Hu Quan memorialized on four matters—the account is given in the "Biography of Hu Quan."

sentences.zh: 除侍御史，上謂胡銓曰：「比除臺官，外議如何？」

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant Censor, and the emperor said to Hu Quan: "How has outside opinion received the recent appointments to the Censorate?"
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed attendant censor, and the emperor said to Hu Quan, "What is outside opinion of the recent appointments to the Censorate?"

sentences.zh: 銓曰：「皆謂得人。」

translations.literal: Quan said: "All say worthy men have been obtained."
translations.idiomatic: Quan said, "All agree that worthy men have been found."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿與十朋皆朕親擢。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You and Shipeng were both personally promoted by me."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You and Shipeng were both personally selected by me."

sentences.zh: 十朋見上英銳，每見必陳恢復之計。

translations.literal: Shipeng saw that the emperor was spirited and sharp; whenever he had audience he always presented plans for recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Shipeng saw that the emperor was spirited and resolute; whenever he had audience he always presented plans for national recovery.

sentences.zh: 及將北伐，上疏曰：

translations.literal: When the northern expedition was about to be launched, he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: When the northern expedition was about to be launched, he submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 「天子之孝莫大於光祖宗、安社稷，因前王盈成而守者，周成康、漢文景是也；

translations.literal: "Of filial piety in a Son of Heaven, nothing is greater than glorifying the ancestors and securing the altars of state. Those who, inheriting the full accomplishment of former kings, preserved it are King Cheng and King Kang of Zhou and Emperors Wen and Jing of Han;
translations.idiomatic: "Of filial piety in a Son of Heaven, nothing is greater than glorifying the ancestors and securing the altars of state. Those who inherited a flourishing legacy and preserved it include King Cheng and King Kang of Zhou and Emperors Wen and Jing of Han;

sentences.zh: 承前世衰微而興者，商高宗、周宣王是也；

translations.literal: those who, inheriting the decline of former ages, rose up are King Gaozong of Shang and King Xuan of Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: those who rose from the decline of a former age include King Gaozong of Shang and King Xuan of Zhou;

sentences.zh: 先君有恥而雪之，漢宣帝臣單于、唐太宗俘頡利是也；

translations.literal: those who, when the former ruler had shame, wiped it away are Emperor Xuan of Han, who made the Xiongnu chanyu his minister, and Emperor Taizong of Tang, who captured Jieli;
translations.idiomatic: those who wiped away a former ruler's shame include Emperor Xuan of Han, who made the Xiongnu chanyu his minister, and Emperor Taizong of Tang, who captured Jieli;

sentences.zh: 先君有仇而復之，夏少康滅澆、漢光武誅莽是也。

translations.literal: those who, when the former ruler had an enemy, took revenge are Shaokang of Xia, who destroyed Ao, and Emperor Guangwu of Han, who executed Wang Mang.
translations.idiomatic: those who avenged a former ruler's enemy include Shaokang of Xia, who destroyed Ao, and Emperor Guangwu of Han, who executed Wang Mang.

sentences.zh: 跡雖不同，其為孝一也。

translations.literal: Though the tracks differ, their filial piety is one.
translations.idiomatic: Though the paths differ, the filial duty is the same.

sentences.zh: 靖康之禍，亙古未有，陛下英武，慨然志在興復。

translations.literal: The calamity of the Jingkang era was without precedent since antiquity; Your Majesty is spirited and martial, and resolutely sets his will on restoration.
translations.idiomatic: The calamity of the Jingkang era was without precedent in history. Your Majesty is spirited and martial, and resolutely sets his heart on restoration.

sentences.zh: 竊聞每對群臣奏事，則曰：『當如創業時。』

translations.literal: I have heard that whenever Your Majesty addresses the assembled ministers, you say: "We must act as at the time of founding the dynasty."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that whenever Your Majesty addresses the assembled ministers, you say, "We must act as we did when the dynasty was first founded."

sentences.zh: 又曰：『當以馬上治之。』

translations.literal: You also say: "We must govern from horseback."
translations.idiomatic: You also say, "We must govern from horseback."

sentences.zh: 又曰：『某事當俟恢復後為之』。

translations.literal: You also say: "A certain matter must wait until after recovery."
translations.idiomatic: You also say, "Certain matters must wait until after recovery."

sentences.zh: 比因宣召，語及陵寢，聖容惻然，曰：『四十年矣。』

translations.literal: Recently, because of an imperial summons, the conversation touched on the imperial tombs; the sacred countenance was deeply moved, and you said: "Forty years have passed."
translations.idiomatic: Recently, in an imperial audience, the conversation turned to the imperial tombs. Your countenance grew sorrowful, and you said, "Forty years have passed."

sentences.zh: 陛下之心真少康、高宗、宣王、光武之心，奈何大臣不能仰副聖心？

translations.literal: Your Majesty's heart is truly the heart of Shaokang, Gaozong, Xuanwang, and Guangwu—yet how is it that the great ministers cannot lift themselves to match the sacred heart?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's heart is truly the heart of Shaokang, Gaozong, Xuanwang, and Guangwu—yet how is it that the great ministers cannot rise to match your resolve?

sentences.zh: 願戒在位者，去附和之私心，贊國家之大計，則中興日月可冀矣。」

translations.literal: I wish that those in office be warned to cast off the private mind of mere agreement, and support the great plan of the state—then the day of revival may be hoped for."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that those in office be warned to cast off the private habit of mere agreement and support the nation's great plan of recovery—then the day of revival may truly be hoped for."

sentences.zh: 因論史浩八罪，曰懷奸、誤國、植黨、盜權、忌言、蔽賢、欺君、訕上，上為出浩知紹興府。

translations.literal: He then discussed eight crimes of Shi Hao, saying: harboring treachery, harming the state, forming factions, usurping power, resenting speech, obscuring the worthy, deceiving the ruler, and insulting the sovereign; the emperor therefore sent Hao out to serve as prefect of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: He then enumerated eight crimes of Shi Hao: harboring treachery, harming the state, forming factions, usurping power, resenting free speech, obscuring the worthy, deceiving the ruler, and insulting the sovereign. The emperor thereupon sent Hao out to serve as prefect of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 十朋再疏，謂：「陛下雖能如舜之去邪，未能如舜之正名定罪。

translations.literal: Shipeng submitted another memorial, saying: "Although Your Majesty can remove the wicked as Shun did, you have not yet been able, as Shun did, to rectify names and fix guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Shipeng submitted another memorial, saying, "Although Your Majesty can remove the wicked as Shun did, you have not yet been able, as Shun did, to rectify names and fix guilt upon them.

sentences.zh: 紹興密邇行都，浩嘗為屬吏，姦賍彰聞，亦何顏復見其吏民。」

translations.literal: Shaoxing is close to the traveling capital; Hao was once a subordinate official there, and his corruption and guilt are publicly known—how can he bear again to face its clerks and people?"
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxing lies close to the traveling capital. Hao once served there as a subordinate official, and his corruption is publicly known. How can he bear to face its clerks and people again?"

sentences.zh: 遂改與祠。

translations.literal: He was thereupon changed to temple appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was thereupon given a temple appointment instead.

sentences.zh: 史正志與浩族異，拜浩而父事之，十朋論正志傾險奸姦，觀時求進，宜黜正志以正典刑。

translations.literal: Shi Zhengzhi, though of a different clan from Hao, bowed to Hao and treated him as a father; Shipeng argued that Zhengzhi was overbearing, treacherous, and wicked, watching the times to advance, and that Zhengzhi should be dismissed to uphold the proper punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhengzhi, though not of Hao's clan, bowed to Hao and treated him as a father. Shipeng argued that Zhengzhi was overbearing, treacherous, and wicked, watching the times to advance, and that he should be dismissed to uphold the proper punishments.

sentences.zh: 林安宅出入史浩、龍大淵門，盜弄威福，至是詐病求致仕，十朋並疏其罪。

translations.literal: Lin Anzhai moved in and out of the gates of Shi Hao and Long Dayuan, usurping and manipulating authority and favor; at this time he feigned illness and sought retirement; Shipeng also memorialized his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Anzhai moved in and out of the households of Shi Hao and Long Dayuan, usurping and manipulating authority and favor. At this time he feigned illness and sought retirement; Shipeng also memorialized his crimes.

sentences.zh: 皆罷去。

translations.literal: All were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: All were dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 張浚出師復靈壁、虹縣，歸附者萬計，又復宿州。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun marched out and recovered Lingbi and Hong County; those who submitted numbered in the tens of thousands, and he also recovered Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun marched out and recovered Lingbi and Hong County; those who submitted numbered in the tens of thousands, and he also recovered Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 十朋奏：「王師以吊民為主，先之以招納，不獲已而戰伐隨之，乞以此指戒浚。

translations.literal: Shipeng memorialized: "The imperial army should take succoring the people as its main purpose, first using recruitment and submission; only when that fails should warfare follow. I ask that this instruction be given to Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Shipeng memorialized, "The imperial army should take succoring the people as its main purpose, beginning with recruitment and submission and resorting to warfare only when necessary. I ask that this instruction be sent to Jun.

sentences.zh: 金將既降，宜速加爵賞，以勸來者。」

translations.literal: When Jin generals have already surrendered, ranks and rewards should quickly be added to encourage those who come afterward."
translations.idiomatic: When Jin generals have already surrendered, ranks and rewards should quickly be granted to encourage others to follow."

sentences.zh: 上皆嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted all of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted all of this.

sentences.zh: 會李顯忠、邵宏淵不協，王師失律，張浚上表自劾，主和者乘此唱異議。

translations.literal: When Li Xianzhong and Shao Hongyuan failed to cooperate, the imperial army lost discipline; Zhang Jun submitted a memorial impeaching himself, and those favoring peace seized the moment to raise dissenting views.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xianzhong and Shao Hongyuan failed to cooperate, the imperial army lost discipline. Zhang Jun submitted a memorial impeaching himself, and those favoring peace seized the moment to raise dissenting views.

sentences.zh: 十朋上疏言：「臣素不識浚，聞其誓不與敵俱生，心實慕之。

translations.literal: Shipeng submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject has never known Jun personally, but hearing that he swore he would not live together with the enemy, your subject truly admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Shipeng submitted a memorial saying, "I have never known Jun personally, but hearing that he swore he would not live together with the enemy, I truly admired him.

sentences.zh: 前因輪對，言金必敗盟，乞用浚。

translations.literal: Previously, in a rotating memorial, I said the Jin would surely break the alliance and begged that Jun be employed.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, in a rotating memorial, I said the Jin would surely break the alliance and begged that Jun be employed.

sentences.zh: 陛下嗣位，命督師江、淮，今浚遣將取二縣，一月三捷，皆服陛下任浚之難。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty succeeded to the throne, you ordered him to supervise the Jiang and Huai armies; now Jun sent generals to take two counties and in one month achieved three victories—all submit to the difficulty of Your Majesty's entrusting Jun.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty succeeded to the throne, you ordered him to supervise the Jiang and Huai armies. Now Jun has sent generals to take two counties and in one month achieved three victories—all acknowledge the wisdom of Your Majesty's trust in Jun.

sentences.zh: 及王師一不利，橫議蜂起。

translations.literal: When the imperial army suffered one setback, wild talk swarmed forth.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army suffered one setback, wild talk swarmed forth.

sentences.zh: 臣謂今日之師，為祖宗陵寢，為二帝復仇，為二百年境土，為中原弔民伐罪，非前代好大生事者比。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that today's campaign is for the imperial tombs of the ancestors, to avenge the two emperors, for two hundred years of territory, and to succor the people of the Central Plains and punish crime—it is not to be compared with former ages' lovers of war and creators of trouble.
translations.idiomatic: I consider that today's campaign is fought for the imperial tombs of the ancestors, to avenge the two emperors, for two hundred years of territory, and to succor the people of the Central Plains and punish wrongdoing—it cannot be compared with the war-loving troublemakers of former ages.

sentences.zh: 益當內修，俟時而動。

translations.literal: All the more should we cultivate ourselves internally and wait for the right moment to act.
translations.idiomatic: All the more should we strengthen ourselves internally and wait for the right moment to act.

sentences.zh: 陛下恢復志立，固不以一衄為群議所搖，然異論紛紛，浚既待罪，臣其可尚居風憲之職！

translations.literal: Your Majesty's will for recovery is established and will surely not be shaken by one defeat in the clamor of diverse opinion; yet dissenting views are numerous and confused, and since Jun already awaits punishment, how can your subject still remain in the office of censorial integrity!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's will for recovery is firm and will surely not be shaken by one defeat amid clamoring dissent; yet opposing views multiply, and since Jun already awaits punishment, how can I still remain in the office of censorial integrity!

sentences.zh: 乞賜竄殛。」

translations.literal: I beg to be banished and executed."
translations.idiomatic: I beg to be banished or executed."

sentences.zh: 因言：「臣聞近日欲遣龍大淵撫諭淮南，信否？」

translations.literal: He then said: "Your subject has heard that recently there is a plan to send Long Dayuan to pacify and instruct Huainan—is this true?"
translations.idiomatic: He then added, "I have heard that recently there is a plan to send Long Dayuan to pacify and instruct Huainan—is this true?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「無之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "There is nothing of the sort."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "No, there is not."

sentences.zh: 又言：「聞欲以楊存中充御營使。」

translations.literal: He also said: "I have heard that Yang Cunzhong is to be appointed Commissioner of the Imperial Camp."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "I have heard that Yang Cunzhong is to be appointed Imperial Camp Commissioner."

sentences.zh: 上嘿然。

translations.literal: The Emperor fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 改除吏部侍郎，力辭，出知饒州。

translations.literal: He was transferred and appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, but fervently declined; he was sent out as prefect of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice minister of personnel but fervently declined and was sent out to serve as prefect of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 饒並湖，盜出沒其間，聞十朋至，一夕遁去。

translations.literal: Raozhou bordered the lake; bandits appeared and vanished there. When they heard Shipeng had arrived, in one night they fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Raozhou bordered the lake, and bandits roamed the area. When they heard that Shipeng had arrived, they fled overnight.

sentences.zh: 丞相洪适請故學基益其圃，十朋曰：「先聖所居，十朋何敢予人。」

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Hong Shi requested the old academy grounds to expand his garden. Shipeng said: "The place where the Former Sage dwelt—how would Shipeng dare give it to another?"
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Hong Shi asked for the old academy grounds to enlarge his garden. Shipeng said, "The place where the Former Sage lived—how could I give it away?"

sentences.zh: 移知夔州，饒民走諸司乞留不得，至斷其橋，乃以車從間道去，眾葺斷橋，以「王公」名之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Kui Prefecture. The people of Raozhou ran to various offices begging to keep him but could not; they even broke the bridge. He then left by carriage by a hidden path. The people rebuilt the broken bridge and named it "Lord Wang."
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Kui Prefecture. The people of Raozhou petitioned every office to keep him, to no avail; they even broke the bridge. He left by carriage along a back road. The people rebuilt the bridge and named it "Lord Wang."

sentences.zh: 移知湖州，召對，劉珙請留之，上曰：「朕豈不知王十朋，顧湖州被水，非十朋莫能鎮撫。」

translations.literal: He was transferred to Huzhou. Summoned for audience, Liu Bing asked to keep him. The Emperor said: "Do I not know Wang Shipeng? But Huzhou has been flooded—only Shipeng can pacify and reassure it."
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Huzhou, he was summoned for an audience. Liu Bing asked that he be kept at court. The Emperor said, "Do I not know Wang Shipeng? But Huzhou has been inundated—only Shipeng can pacify and reassure the people there."

sentences.zh: 至郡，戶部責虛逋三十四萬，命吏持券往辨，不聽，即請祠去。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the prefecture, the Ministry of Revenue held him responsible for 340,000 in spurious arrears. He sent an official with vouchers to dispute it, but they would not listen. He immediately requested temple leave and departed.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the prefecture, the Ministry of Revenue charged him with 340,000 in false arrears. He sent an official with vouchers to dispute the claim, but they refused to hear him. He immediately requested temple leave and left.

sentences.zh: 起知泉州，十朋前在湖割奉錢創貢闈，又為泉建之，尤宏壯。

translations.literal: He was reappointed prefect of Quanzhou. Shipeng had previously in Huzhou cut from his salary to build the examination hall; he built one for Quanzhou as well, even more grand and imposing.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Quanzhou. Shipeng had earlier in Huzhou cut from his own salary to build an examination hall; he built one for Quanzhou as well, even more grand and imposing.

sentences.zh: 凡歷四郡，布上恩，恤民隱，士之賢者詣門，以禮致之。

translations.literal: In all he governed four prefectures, spreading imperial grace and caring for the people's hidden grievances. Worthy scholars who came to his door he received with proper courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: In all he governed four prefectures, spreading the emperor's grace and tending to the people's hidden grievances. Worthy scholars who came to his door he received with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 朔望會諸生學宮，講經詢政，僚屬間有不善，反復告戒，俾之自新。

translations.literal: On the first and fifteenth of each month he gathered students at the Confucian school, lecturing on the classics and inquiring into governance. When subordinates occasionally fell short, he repeatedly admonished them and urged them to reform.
translations.idiomatic: On the first and fifteenth of each month he gathered students at the county school, lecturing on the classics and inquiring into local governance. When subordinates fell short, he admonished them again and again until they reformed.

sentences.zh: 民輸租俾自概量，聞者相告，宿逋亦願償。

translations.literal: He had the people pay rent taxes by measuring grain themselves. Those who heard this told one another, and even long-standing arrears were willingly repaid.
translations.idiomatic: He let the people measure their own grain when paying rent taxes. Word spread among them, and even long-standing arrears were willingly repaid.

sentences.zh: 訟至庭，溫詞曉以理義，多退聽者。

translations.literal: When lawsuits came to court, he used gentle words to instruct them in reason and principle; many litigants withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When lawsuits came to court, he used gentle words to explain reason and principle, and many litigants withdrew their cases.

sentences.zh: 所至人繪而祠之，去之日，老稚攀留涕泣，越境以送，思之如父母。

translations.literal: Wherever he went, people painted his likeness and worshipped him. On the day he left, old and young clung to him weeping; they escorted him beyond the border, missing him as they would their own parents.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went, people painted his likeness and enshrined him. When he departed, old and young clung to him in tears and escorted him beyond the border, cherishing him as they would their own parents.

sentences.zh: 饒久旱，入境雨至；

translations.literal: Raozhou had long suffered drought; when he entered its borders, rain came.
translations.idiomatic: Raozhou had long suffered drought; rain fell as soon as he entered its borders.

sentences.zh: 湖積霖，入境即霽。

translations.literal: Huzhou had accumulated long rains; as soon as he entered, the skies cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Huzhou had endured prolonged rains; the skies cleared the moment he entered.

sentences.zh: 凡禱必應，其至誠不獨感人，而亦動天地鬼神。

translations.literal: Every prayer was answered. His utmost sincerity moved not only men but also Heaven, Earth, and the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Every prayer he offered was answered. His utmost sincerity moved not only people but Heaven, Earth, and the spirits as well.

sentences.zh: 東宮建，除太子詹事，力辭，詔州郡禮致，遂力疾造朝，以足疾不能趨，詔給扶減拜。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Palace was established, he was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent. He fervently declined. An edict ordered the prefecture to escort him with ceremony. He then forced himself, though ill, to come to court. Because of foot ailment he could not hurry; an edict granted him a staff and reduced bows.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Palace was established, he was appointed grand mentor of the heir apparent but fervently declined. An edict ordered the prefecture to escort him to court with ceremony. He then came despite serious illness. Because foot ailment kept him from hurrying, an edict granted him a staff and reduced the number of bows required.

sentences.zh: 謁東宮，太子以其舊學，待遇有加。

translations.literal: On visiting the Eastern Palace, the Crown Prince, because he had been his former teacher, treated him with special honor.
translations.idiomatic: When he visited the Eastern Palace, the crown prince treated him with special honor, for he had once been his teacher.

sentences.zh: 又詔免朝參，遣中使以告及襲衣、金帶就其家賜之。

translations.literal: An edict also exempted him from court attendance. The Emperor sent a palace envoy to inform him and bestowed formal robes and a gold belt at his home.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also exempted him from court attendance. The emperor sent a palace envoy to notify him and bestowed court robes and a gold belt at his home.

sentences.zh: 疾革，累章告老，以龍圖閣學士致仕，命下而卒，年六十。

translations.literal: When his illness became critical, he repeatedly memorialized to retire. He retired as Hanlin Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall. The order had just been issued when he died, at age sixty.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness turned critical, he repeatedly memorialized to retire. He was granted retirement as Hanlin academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall. The order had just been issued when he died, at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 紹熙三年，諡曰「忠文」。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaoxi, he was posthumously given the title "Loyal and Refined."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Shaoxi reign, he was posthumously given the posthumous title "Loyal and Refined."

sentences.zh: 十朋事親孝，終喪不處內，友愛二弟，郊恩先奏其名，沒而二子猶布衣。

translations.literal: Shipeng was filial to his parents. Throughout mourning he did not live within his quarters. He was loving to his two younger brothers; at suburban amnesties he first submitted their names. After his death his two sons still wore common cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Shipeng was filial toward his parents and, throughout mourning, did not live within the inner quarters. He was affectionate toward his two younger brothers and, at suburban amnesties, submitted their names first. After his death his two sons still wore plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 書室扁曰「不欺」，每以諸葛亮、顏真卿、寇準、范仲淹、韓琦、唐介自比，朱熹、張栻雅敬之。

translations.literal: His study was inscribed "No Deception." He often compared himself to Zhuge Liang, Yan Zhenqing, Kou Zhun, Fan Zhongyan, Han Qi, and Tang Jie. Zhu Xi and Zhang Shi held him in deep respect.
translations.idiomatic: His study bore the inscription "No Deception." He often measured himself against Zhuge Liang, Yan Zhenqing, Kou Zhun, Fan Zhongyan, Han Qi, and Tang Jie. Zhu Xi and Zhang Shi held him in deep respect.

sentences.zh: 子聞詩、聞禮，皆篤學自立。

translations.literal: His sons Wen Shi and Wen Li were both earnest scholars who stood on their own.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Wen Shi and Wen Li were both earnest scholars who stood on their own merit.

sentences.zh: 聞詩知光州、提點江東刑獄；

translations.literal: Wen Shi served as prefect of Guang Prefecture and as Judicial Commissioner for Jiangdong Circuit;
translations.idiomatic: Wen Shi served as prefect of Guang Prefecture and as judicial commissioner for Jiangdong Circuit;

sentences.zh: 聞禮知常州、江東轉運判官，為治能守家法，人亦思慕之。

translations.literal: Wen Li served as prefect of Changzhou and as Vice Transport Commissioner for Jiangdong; in governance he could uphold the family way, and people also admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Li served as prefect of Changzhou and as vice transport commissioner for Jiangdong. In governing he upheld the family tradition, and people admired him as well.

sentences.zh: 吳芾，字明可，台州仙居人。

translations.literal: Wu Fei, styled Mingke, was a native of Xianju in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fei, whose style name was Mingke, was a native of Xianju in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 舉進士第，遷秘書正字。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was promoted to Corrector in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was promoted to corrector in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 與秦檜舊故，至是檜已專政，芾退然如未嘗識。

translations.literal: He had been an old acquaintance of Qin Hui. By this time Qin Hui already monopolized power; Fei withdrew humbly as if they had never known each other.
translations.idiomatic: He had been an old acquaintance of Qin Hui, but by then Qin Hui already monopolized power, and Fei withdrew humbly as though they had never known each other.

sentences.zh: 公坐旅進，揖而退，檜疑之，風言者論罷。

translations.literal: At a public gathering they advanced together; Fei bowed and withdrew. Qin Hui was suspicious and had memorialists attack him until he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: At a public gathering they advanced together; Fei bowed and withdrew. Qin Hui grew suspicious and had memorialists attack him until he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 通判處、婺、越三郡。

translations.literal: He served as vice prefect of Chu, Wu, and Yue prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice prefect of Chu, Wu, and Yue.

sentences.zh: 知處州。

translations.literal: He was prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 處舊苦丁絹重，芾損之，以新丁補其額。

translations.literal: Chuzhou had long suffered from heavy corvée silk levies. Fei reduced them, supplementing the quota with new households registered for corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhou had long suffered from heavy corvée silk levies. Fei reduced the burden, making up the quota with newly registered households.

sentences.zh: 何溥薦芾材中御史，除監察御史。

translations.literal: He Bo recommended Fei as qualified for censor and he was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He Bo recommended Fei as qualified to serve as censor, and he was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 時金將敗盟，芾勸高宗「專務修德，痛自悔咎，延見群臣，俾陳闕失，求合乎天地，無愧乎祖宗，則人心悅服，天亦助順矣。」

translations.literal: When the Jin were about to break the treaty, Fei urged Emperor Gaozong: "Devote yourself solely to cultivating virtue, deeply repent your errors, summon the ministers, and have them state failures—seek to accord with Heaven and Earth and be worthy before your ancestors; then hearts will be pleased and Heaven too will aid the righteous cause."
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin were about to break the treaty, Fei urged Emperor Gaozong, "Devote yourself solely to cultivating virtue, repent your errors deeply, summon your ministers, and have them state what is lacking. Seek to accord with Heaven and Earth and stand without shame before your ancestors, and hearts will be won and Heaven will aid the righteous cause."

sentences.zh: 上韙其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his words.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace censor.

sentences.zh: 兩淮戰不利，廷臣爭陳退避計，芾言：「今日之事，有進無退，進為上策，退為無策。」

translations.literal: When warfare in the Two Huai regions went badly, court ministers competed to propose plans of retreat. Fei said: "In today's situation there is advance but no retreat. Advance is the superior strategy; retreat is no strategy at all."
translations.idiomatic: When warfare in the Two Huai regions went badly, court ministers competed to propose plans of retreat. Fei said, "In today's situation there is advance but no retreat. Advance is the superior strategy; retreat is no strategy at all."

sentences.zh: 既而金主亮斃，上疏勸親征。

translations.literal: Shortly after, the Jin ruler Hailing was killed. Fei submitted a memorial urging the Emperor to campaign in person.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the Jin ruler Hailing was killed, and Fei submitted a memorial urging the emperor to campaign in person.

sentences.zh: 車駕至建康，芾請遂駐蹕，以係中原之望，高宗納其說。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage reached Jiankang, Fei requested that it remain there to sustain the hopes of the Central Plains. Gaozong accepted his view.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage reached Jiankang, Fei asked that it remain there to sustain the hopes of the Central Plains, and Gaozong accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 會有密啟還東者，下侍從、臺諫議，芾言：「今欲控帶襄、漢，引輸湖、廣，則臨安不如建康便；

translations.literal: When someone secretly memorialized to return east, the matter was sent down for discussion among attendants and censorial remonstrators. Fei said: "If we now wish to control the Xiang and Han regions and draw supplies from Hunan and Guangdong, then Lin'an is less convenient than Jiankang;
translations.idiomatic: When someone secretly memorialized to return east, the matter was sent down for discussion among attendants and remonstrating censors. Fei said, "If we now wish to control the Xiang and Han regions and draw supplies from Hunan and Guangdong, then Lin'an is less convenient than Jiankang;

sentences.zh: 經理淮甸，應接梁、宋，則臨安不如建康近。

translations.literal: If we wish to manage the Huai region and respond to Liang and Song, then Lin'an is not as close as Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: if we wish to manage the Huai region and respond to Liang and Song, then Lin'an is not as close as Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 議者徒悅一時扈從思歸之人，非為國計。

translations.literal: Those debating the issue merely please those who attend the emperor and long to return home for the moment—they do not consider the nation's interest.
translations.idiomatic: Those debating the issue merely please those who attend the emperor and long to return home for the moment; they do not consider the nation's interest.

sentences.zh: 臣恐回鑾之後，西師之聲援不接，北土之謳吟絕望矣。」

translations.literal: Your subject fears that after the imperial return east, western armies will receive no support and the songs of longing from the northern lands will die in despair."
translations.idiomatic: I fear that after the imperial return east, western armies will receive no support and the songs of longing from the northern lands will die in despair."

sentences.zh: 又言：「去歲兩淮諸城望風奔潰，無一城能拒守者，此秦檜壅塞言路、挫折士氣之餘毒也。

translations.literal: He also said: "Last year the cities of the Two Huai fled and collapsed at the mere rumor of attack—not one city could hold fast. This is the lingering poison of Qin Hui's blocking of speech and crushing of morale.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Last year the cities of the Two Huai fled and collapsed at the mere rumor of attack—not one city could hold fast. This is the lingering poison of Qin Hui's blocking of speech and crushing of morale.

sentences.zh: 能反其道，則士氣日振，而見危授命者有人矣。」

translations.literal: If we reverse that course, morale will daily rise, and men who meet danger and give their lives will appear."
translations.idiomatic: If we reverse that course, morale will rise day by day, and men who meet danger and give their lives will appear."

sentences.zh: 知婺州。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Wu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 孝宗初即位，陛辭，陳裴垍對唐憲宗「為治先正其心」，以為臨御之初，出治大原，無越於此。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong had just ascended the throne, Fei took leave at court and cited Pei Ji's words to Tang Xianzong: "In governing, first rectify the heart," holding that at the outset of imperial rule there was no governing principle more fundamental than this.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong had just ascended the throne, Fei took leave at court and cited Pei Ji's words to Tang Xianzong: "In governing, first rectify the heart," holding that at the outset of imperial rule there was no governing principle more fundamental than this.

sentences.zh: 上嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 至郡，勸民義役。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the prefecture, he encouraged the people to practice voluntary corvée service.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching the prefecture, he encouraged the people to practice voluntary corvée service.

sentences.zh: 金華長仙鄉民十有一家，自以甲乙第其產，相次執役，幾二十年。

translations.literal: In Changxian Township of Jinhua, eleven households had ranked their property in gradations A and B and taken turns performing corvée service for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: In Changxian Township of Jinhua, eleven households had ranked their property in gradations A and B and taken turns performing corvée service for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 芾輿致十一人者，與合宴，更其鄉曰「循理」，里曰「信義」，以褒異之。

translations.literal: Fei had the eleven men conveyed by carriage to join him in a feast together, renamed their township "Following Principle" and their village "Trust and Righteousness," to honor and distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: Fei had the eleven men conveyed by carriage to join him in a feast, renamed their township "Following Principle" and their village "Trust and Righteousness," to honor and distinguish them.

sentences.zh: 知紹興府。

translations.literal: He was prefect of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 會稽賦重而折色尤甚，芾以攢宮在，奏免支移折變。

translations.literal: Kuaiji's tax burdens were heavy, and conversion surcharges especially severe. Because the imperial tombs were there, Fei memorialized to exempt transport conversion charges.
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji's tax burdens were heavy, and conversion surcharges especially severe. Because the imperial tombs were located there, Fei memorialized to exempt transport and conversion charges.

sentences.zh: 鑒湖久廢，會歲大饑，出常平米募饑民浚治。

translations.literal: Mirror Lake had long fallen into disuse. When a great famine struck, he released Ever-Normal Granary rice and hired hungry people to dredge and restore it.
translations.idiomatic: Mirror Lake had long fallen into disuse. When a great famine struck, he released Ever-Normal Granary rice and hired hungry people to dredge and restore it.

sentences.zh: 芾去，大姓利於田，湖復廢。

translations.literal: After Fei left, great clans profited from the farmland and the lake was abandoned again.
translations.idiomatic: After Fei left, powerful clans profited from the farmland and the lake was abandoned once more.

sentences.zh: 權刑部侍郎，遷給事中，改吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Acting Vice Minister of Justice, he was transferred to Recipient of Edicts, then changed to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as acting vice minister of justice, he was transferred to recipient of edicts and then reassigned as vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 以敷文閣直學士知臨安府。

translations.literal: As Academician of the Hall for the Diffusion of Literature he was prefect of Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: As academician of the Hall for the Diffusion of Literature, he served as prefect of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 內侍家僮毆傷酒家保，芾捕治之，徇于市，權豪側目。

translations.literal: A palace eunuch's household servant beat and injured a tavern keeper. Fei arrested and punished him, displaying the punishment in the market. The powerful glared.
translations.idiomatic: A palace eunuch's household servant beat and injured a tavern keeper. Fei arrested and punished him and had the sentence displayed in the market, to the fury of the powerful.

sentences.zh: 執政議以芾使金，復除吏部侍郎，且議以龍大淵為副，芾曰：「是可與言行事者邪？」

translations.literal: The chief ministers proposed sending Fei as envoy to Jin. He was again appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, and they also proposed Long Dayuan as deputy. Fei said: "Is this someone with whom one can act in good faith?"
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers proposed sending Fei as envoy to the Jin. He was again appointed vice minister of personnel, and they also proposed Long Dayuan as his deputy. Fei said, "Is this someone with whom one can act in good faith?"

sentences.zh: 語聞，得罷不行。

translations.literal: When his words were reported, the mission was cancelled and he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When his words were reported, the mission was cancelled and he did not go.

sentences.zh: 下遷禮部侍郎，力求去，提舉太平興國宮。

translations.literal: Demoted to Vice Minister of Rites, he earnestly sought to leave and was made Superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Demoted to vice minister of rites, he earnestly sought to leave office and was appointed superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.

sentences.zh: 時芾與陳俊卿俱以剛直見忌，未幾，俊卿亦引去。

translations.literal: At the time Fei and Chen Junqing were both resented for their firm uprightness. Before long Junqing also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Fei and Chen Junqing were both resented for their firm uprightness. Before long Junqing withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人閻安中為孝宗言二臣之去，非國之福。

translations.literal: Secretariat Drafter Yan Anzhong told Xiaozong that the departure of these two ministers was no blessing to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat drafter Yan Anzhong told Emperor Xiaozong that the departure of these two ministers was no blessing to the state.

sentences.zh: 起知太平州。

translations.literal: He was recalled as prefect of Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Taiping.

sentences.zh: 造舟以梁姑溪。

translations.literal: He built boats to bridge the Guxi River.
translations.idiomatic: He built boats to bridge the Guxi River.

sentences.zh: 歷陽築者久役潰歸，聲言欲趨郡境，芾呼至城下，厚犒遣之，而密捕倡亂者繫獄以聞，詔褒諭。

translations.literal: Laborers from Liyang who had long served on construction projects broke and returned home, declaring they would march on the prefecture. Fei summoned them below the city wall, rewarded them generously and sent them away, while secretly arresting ringleaders and imprisoning them; he reported this and received an edict of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Laborers from Liyang who had long served on construction projects broke ranks and returned home, declaring they would march on the prefecture. Fei summoned them below the city wall, rewarded them generously, and sent them away, while secretly arresting the ringleaders and imprisoning them. He reported this to the throne and received an edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 知隆興府。

translations.literal: He was prefect of Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Longxing.

sentences.zh: 芾前後守六郡，各因其俗為寬猛，吏莫容姦，民懷惠利。

translations.literal: Fei successively governed six prefectures, adjusting strictness or leniency to local custom. Officials could conceal no fraud; the people felt his benevolence and benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Fei successively governed six prefectures, adjusting strictness and leniency to local custom. Officials could conceal no fraud, and the people felt his benevolence and benefit.

sentences.zh: 再奉太平祠，屢告老，以龍圖閣直學士致仕。

translations.literal: He again took charge of the Taiping temple service, repeatedly memorialized to retire, and retired as Hanlin Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He again took charge of the Taiping temple service, repeatedly memorialized to retire, and retired as Hanlin academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 後十年卒，年八十。

translations.literal: Ten years later he died, at age eighty.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years later he died, at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「視官物當如己物，視公事當如私事。

translations.literal: He once said: "Treat official property as one's own property; treat public affairs as private affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Treat official property as your own property, and treat public affairs as private affairs.

sentences.zh: 與其得罪于百姓，寧得罪于上官。」

translations.literal: Rather offend one's superiors than offend the common people."
translations.idiomatic: Better to offend your superiors than to offend the common people."

sentences.zh: 立朝不偶，晚退閑者十有四年，自號「湖山居士」。

translations.literal: He was ill-fated at court; in his later years he retired in leisure for fourteen years and styled himself "Recluse of Lakes and Mountains."
translations.idiomatic: Ill-fated at court, he spent the last fourteen years of his life in retirement and styled himself "Recluse of Lakes and Mountains."

sentences.zh: 為文豪健俊整，有表奏五卷、詩文三十卷。

translations.literal: His writing was bold, vigorous, and finely ordered. He left five fascicles of memorials and thirty fascicles of poetry and prose.
translations.idiomatic: His writing was bold, vigorous, and finely ordered. He left five fascicles of memorials and thirty fascicles of poetry and prose.

sentences.zh: 陳良翰

translations.literal: Chen Lianghan
translations.idiomatic: Chen Lianghan

sentences.zh: 陳良翰，字邦彥，台州臨海人。

translations.literal: Chen Lianghan, styled Bangyan, was a native of Linhai in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Lianghan, whose style name was Bangyan, was a native of Linhai in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 蚤孤，事母孝。

translations.literal: Orphaned early, he was filial to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, he was filial toward his mother.

sentences.zh: 資莊重，為文恢博有氣。

translations.literal: By nature solemn and dignified, his writing was broad, expansive, and spirited.
translations.idiomatic: By nature solemn and dignified, he wrote in a broad, expansive, and spirited style.

sentences.zh: 中紹興五年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Shaoxing reign.

sentences.zh: 知溫州瑞安縣。

translations.literal: He was magistrate of Ruian County in Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Ruian County in Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 俗號強梗，吏治尚嚴，良翰獨撫以寬，催租不下文符，但揭示名物，民競樂輸，聽訟咸得其情。

translations.literal: The local custom was called stubborn and resistant; official rule favored severity. Lianghan alone governed with leniency. For rent collection he issued no formal summons—only posted names and amounts—and the people competed eagerly to pay. In hearing cases he always got to the truth.
translations.idiomatic: The local custom was known for stubborn resistance, and official rule favored severity. Lianghan alone governed with leniency. For rent collection he issued no formal summonses—only posted names and amounts—and the people competed eagerly to pay. In hearing cases he always got to the truth.

sentences.zh: 或問何術，良翰曰：「無術，第公此心如虛堂懸鏡耳。」

translations.literal: When someone asked his method, Lianghan said: "There is no method—only make this heart of yours like a mirror hung in an empty hall."
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked his method, Lianghan said, "There is no method—only make your heart like a mirror hung in an empty hall."

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史吳芾薦為檢法官，遷監察御史。

translations.literal: Palace Censor Wu Fei recommended him as Reviewing Law Officer; he was promoted to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Palace censor Wu Fei recommended him as reviewing law officer, and he was promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 孝宗初元，金主褒新立，求和，而中原舊人多求歸，詔問何以處此，良翰言：「議和，復納降，皆非是。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaozong's reign, the new Jin ruler Bao had just ascended and sought peace, while many old subjects of the Central Plains wished to return. An edict asked how to handle this. Lianghan said: "Discussing peace or accepting surrender again—neither is right.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Xiaozong's reign, the new Jin ruler Bao had just ascended and sought peace, while many old subjects of the Central Plains wished to return. An edict asked how to handle this. Lianghan said, "Discussing peace or accepting surrender again—neither is right.

sentences.zh: 必定計自治，而和不和，任之乃可。」

translations.literal: We must resolve on self-governance; whether there is peace or not, leave it to fate—that is all that will work."
translations.idiomatic: We must resolve on self-governance; whether there is peace or not, leave it to fate—that is all that will work."

sentences.zh: 張浚軍淮、泗以規進取，而議者爭獻防江策，良翰言：「當固藩籬，專委任。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun camped in Huai and Si to plan advances, while debaters competed to offer river-defense strategies. Lianghan said: "We should strengthen the frontier defenses and entrust authority fully.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun camped in Huai and Si to plan advances, while debaters competed to offer river-defense strategies. Lianghan said, "We should strengthen the frontier defenses and entrust authority fully.

sentences.zh: 今舍淮防江，卻地奪便，朝廷過聽，使督府不得專閫外事，誤矣。」

translations.literal: Now to abandon the Huai line to defend the Yangzi—giving up territory and surrendering advantage—because the court listens too readily and will not let the command headquarters manage frontier affairs exclusively, is mistaken."
translations.idiomatic: Now to abandon the Huai line to defend the Yangzi—giving up territory and surrendering advantage—because the court listens too readily and will not let the command headquarters manage frontier affairs exclusively, is mistaken."

sentences.zh: 除右正言。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed right remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 金再移書求故疆，良翰言：「中原皆吾故土，況唐、鄧、海、泗又金渝盟後以兵取之，安得以故疆為言而歸之？」

translations.literal: The Jin again sent letters demanding the old territories. Lianghan said: "The Central Plains are all our old lands. Moreover Tang, Deng, Hai, and Si were taken by Jin by force after they violated the treaty—how can they speak of 'old territories' and demand their return?"
translations.idiomatic: The Jin again sent letters demanding the old territories. Lianghan said, "The Central Plains are all our old lands. Moreover Tang, Deng, Hai, and Si were taken by the Jin by force after they violated the treaty—how can they speak of old territories and demand their return?"

sentences.zh: 湯思退主遣小使盧仲賢、李栻，良翰言：「仲賢輕儇無恥，栻自北來難信。」

translations.literal: Tang Situi advocated sending minor envoys Lu Zhongxian and Li Shi. Lianghan said: "Zhongxian is frivolous and shameless; Shi, coming from the north, is hard to trust."
translations.idiomatic: Tang Situi advocated sending minor envoys Lu Zhongxian and Li Shi. Lianghan said, "Zhongxian is frivolous and shameless; Shi, coming from the north, is hard to trust."

sentences.zh: 又言：「廟堂督府論議不同，邊奏上聞，皆陽唯諾而陰沮敗之。

translations.literal: He also said: "Court and command headquarters disagree in counsel. Border reports sent up are all openly assented to while covertly thwarted and ruined.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Court and command headquarters disagree in counsel. Border reports sent up are all openly assented to while covertly thwarted and ruined.

sentences.zh: 萬一失事機，督府安得獨任其責？」

translations.literal: If by any chance the opportunity is lost, how can the command headquarters alone bear the blame?"
translations.idiomatic: If by any chance the opportunity is lost, how can the command headquarters alone bear the blame?"

sentences.zh: 上矍然稱善。

translations.literal: The Emperor started and praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started and praised this.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣史正志至建康，與張浚議事乖牾，良翰劾之，上曰：「正志亦無罪。」

translations.literal: The court sent Shi Zhengzhi to Jiankang; he clashed with Zhang Jun over policy. Lianghan impeached him. The Emperor said: "Zhengzhi is also not guilty."
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Shi Zhengzhi to Jiankang, where he clashed with Zhang Jun over policy. Lianghan impeached him. The emperor said, "Zhengzhi is also not guilty."

sentences.zh: 良翰言：「陛下使浚守淮，則任浚為重，一郎官為輕，且正志居中，浚必為去就。」

translations.literal: Lianghan said: "Your Majesty stationed Jun to hold the Huai line—then Jun's charge is weighty and a single bureau officer's is light. Moreover, with Zhengzhi at the center, Jun will surely consider leaving his post."
translations.idiomatic: Lianghan said, "Your Majesty stationed Jun to hold the Huai line—then Jun's charge is weighty and a single bureau officer's is light. Moreover, with Zhengzhi at the center, Jun will surely consider leaving his post."

sentences.zh: 上悟，出正志為福建漕運。

translations.literal: The Emperor understood and sent Zhengzhi out as Transport Commissioner for Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood and sent Zhengzhi out as transport commissioner for Fujian.

sentences.zh: 楊存中為御營使，總殿前軍，良翰言：「存中久擅兵柄，太上皇罷就第，奈何復假使名？

translations.literal: Yang Cunzhong was Imperial Camp Commissioner, commanding the Palace Front Army. Lianghan said: "Cunzhong long monopolized military power; the Retired Emperor dismissed him to his residence—why restore to him even a nominal post?
translations.idiomatic: Yang Cunzhong was imperial camp commissioner, commanding the Palace Front Army. Lianghan said, "Cunzhong long monopolized military power; the Retired Emperor dismissed him to his residence—why restore to him even a nominal post?

sentences.zh: 宜慎履霜之戒」疏三上，存中竟罷。

translations.literal: We should heed the warning of treading on frost." After three memorials, Cunzhong was finally dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: We should heed the warning of treading on frost." After three memorials, Cunzhong was finally dismissed."

sentences.zh: 李栻不敢涉淮，良翰奏奪其官。

translations.literal: Li Shi dared not cross the Huai; Lianghan memorialized to strip him of office.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi dared not cross the Huai; Lianghan memorialized to strip him of office.

sentences.zh: 仲賢至汴，輒許金人以疆土、歲幣而還，上大怒，下仲賢吏，欲誅之，宰相叩頭懇請得免。

translations.literal: Zhongxian reached Bian and promptly promised the Jin territory and annual tribute, then returned. The Emperor was furious, had Zhongxian handed to the judicial authorities, and wished to execute him. The chief minister kowtowed and earnestly pleaded until execution was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian reached Bian and promptly promised the Jin territory and annual tribute, then returned. The emperor was furious, had Zhongxian handed over to the judicial authorities, and wished to execute him. The chief minister kowtowed and earnestly pleaded until execution was spared.

sentences.zh: 復遣王之望、龍大淵，良翰言：「前遣使已辱命，大臣不悔前失，不謂秦檜復見今日！

translations.literal: The court again sent Wang Zhiwang and Long Dayuan. Lianghan said: "The previous envoys already disgraced their mission, yet the grand ministers do not repent their earlier failure—I never thought to see Qin Hui alive again today!
translations.idiomatic: The court again sent Wang Zhiwang and Long Dayuan. Lianghan said, "The previous envoys already disgraced their mission, yet the grand ministers do not repent their earlier failure—I never thought to see Qin Hui alive again today!

sentences.zh: 且金要我罷四郡屯兵以歸之，是不折一兵，而坐收四千里要害之地，決不可許。

translations.literal: Moreover the Jin demand that we withdraw garrisons from four prefectures and return them—this is to take four thousand li of strategic land without breaking a single spear. It absolutely must not be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Jin demand that we withdraw garrisons from four prefectures and return them—this is to take four thousand li of strategic land without breaking a single spear. It absolutely must not be granted.

sentences.zh: 若歲幣，則俟得陵寢然後與，庶猶有名。

translations.literal: As for annual tribute, wait until we recover the imperial tombs before paying—then at least there would be some justification.
translations.idiomatic: As for annual tribute, wait until we recover the imperial tombs before paying—then at least there would be some justification.

sentences.zh: 今議未決而之望遂行，恐其辱國不止于仲賢，願先馳一介往，俟議決，行未晚也。」

translations.literal: Now the deliberation is not yet settled yet Zhiwang is already on his way—I fear he will disgrace the state no less than Zhongxian did. I beg that we first dispatch a single envoy; wait until the deliberation is decided, and departure will not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: The court has not yet settled its deliberations, yet Zhiwang is already on his way—I fear he will disgrace the state no less than Zhongxian did. I beg that we first send a single envoy ahead; once the deliberation is decided, it will not be too late to depart."

sentences.zh: 詔侍從、臺諫議，多是良翰，遂以胡昉、楊由義為審議官，與敵議四郡不合，困辱而歸。

translations.literal: An edict ordered attendant officials and censorate-remonstrance officials to discuss; most sided with Lianghan. Hu Fang and Yang Youyi were then appointed review commissioners; they could not agree with the enemy on the four prefectures and returned in distress and humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the attendant officials and censorate-remonstrance officials to deliberate; most sided with Lianghan. Hu Fang and Yang Youyi were then appointed review commissioners, but they could not reach agreement with the enemy over the four prefectures and returned in humiliation.

sentences.zh: 思退尚執前論，正言尹穡附思退以撼督府。

translations.literal: Situi still held to his earlier view; Zhengyan Yin Ji attached himself to Situi to shake the command headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Situi still clung to his earlier view, and Zhengyan Yin Ji attached himself to Situi in order to undermine the command headquarters.

sentences.zh: 良翰為左司諫，疏論：「思退姦邪誤國，宜早罷黜，張浚精忠老謀，不宜以小人言搖之。」

translations.literal: Lianghan served as Left Remonstrance Office censor and memorialized: "Situi is treacherous and wicked and misleads the state—he should be dismissed early. Zhang Jun is loyal in spirit and seasoned in counsel—he should not be shaken by petty men's words."
translations.idiomatic: As left remonstrance office censor, Lianghan submitted a memorial arguing: "Situi is treacherous and wicked and is misleading the state and ought to be dismissed at once, and Zhang Jun, loyal in spirit and seasoned in counsel, ought not be undermined by petty men's words."

sentences.zh: 孝宗曰：「思退前議固失，然朕愛其警敏，冀可效，卿其置之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong said: "Situi's earlier counsel was indeed wrong, yet I value his alert quickness and hope he may yet prove useful—you should let the matter rest.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong said, "Situi's earlier counsel was indeed mistaken, yet I value his quick alertness and hope he may yet prove useful. Let the matter rest.

sentences.zh: 若魏公則今日孰出其右，朕豈容有此意？

translations.literal: As for the Duke of Wei, who today surpasses him? How could I harbor such intent?
translations.idiomatic: As for the Duke of Wei, who today surpasses him? How could I harbor such an intent?

sentences.zh: 縱有之，亦豈不謀卿等？

translations.literal: Even if I did, would I not consult you all?
translations.idiomatic: Even if I did, would I not consult you first?

sentences.zh: 此殆言者有異意，卿為朕諭之。」

translations.literal: This perhaps means the speaker has ulterior intent—you should explain this for me."
translations.idiomatic: This likely means the speaker has ulterior motives—you should explain that to him on my behalf."

sentences.zh: 良翰頓首謝曰：「陛下言及此，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Lianghan kowtowed and thanked him, saying: "Your Majesty speaks of this—all under Heaven are greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Lianghan kowtowed and said in thanks, "Your Majesty speaks of this—the realm is greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 宰相縱無全才，寧取樸實，緩急猶可倚賴。

translations.literal: Even if a chief minister lacks full talent, it is better to choose plain sincerity—in urgent and ordinary times one can still rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: Even if a chief minister lacks every talent, it is better to choose plain sincerity—in times of urgency one can still rely on him.

sentences.zh: 思退庸狡，小黠大癡，將誤國，且「警敏」二字，恐非明主卜相之法。」

translations.literal: Situi is mediocre and cunning—clever in small matters, foolish in great ones—and will mislead the state. Moreover the words "alert quickness" are perhaps not how a wise ruler chooses his ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Situi is mediocre and cunning—clever in small matters but foolish in great ones—and will mislead the state. Moreover, the words "alert quickness" are scarcely how a wise ruler should choose his ministers."

sentences.zh: 既退，以上語諭同列，穡勃然變色，明日亦請對，遂罷良翰言職。

translations.literal: After he withdrew, he relayed the Emperor's words to his colleagues; Ji flushed with anger. The next day he too requested an audience, and Lianghan's remonstrance office post was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After he withdrew, he relayed the emperor's words to his colleagues; Ji flushed with anger. The next day Ji too requested an audience, and Lianghan was dismissed from his remonstrance duties.

sentences.zh: 兩淮既撤備，金大入，孝宗始深悔。

translations.literal: Once the two Huai regions had withdrawn defenses, the Jin invaded on a large scale, and Xiaozong deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Once defenses in the two Huai regions had been withdrawn, the Jin invaded on a large scale, and Xiaozong came to deeply regret it.

sentences.zh: 太學生數百人伏闕，乞召用良翰、胡銓、王十朋而斬思退等，思退由是始敗。

translations.literal: Several hundred Imperial Academy students prostrated themselves at the palace gate, begging to recall Lianghan, Hu Quan, and Wang Shipeng and to execute Situi and others. Situi from this began to fall.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred Imperial Academy students prostrated themselves at the palace gate, begging that Lianghan, Hu Quan, and Wang Shipeng be recalled and Situi and his allies be executed. From this Situi's fortunes began to fail.

sentences.zh: 良翰在諫省，成恭皇后受冊，官內外親屬二十五人，良翰論其冗，詔減七人。

translations.literal: While Lianghan was in the remonstrance offices, when Empress Chenggong received her investiture, twenty-five inner and outer relatives were given office. Lianghan argued this was excessive; an edict reduced it by seven.
translations.idiomatic: While Lianghan served in the remonstrance offices, Empress Chenggong received her investiture and twenty-five relatives inside and outside the clan were granted office. Lianghan argued the appointments were excessive, and an edict reduced them by seven.

sentences.zh: 知建寧府、福建轉運副使，提點江東刑獄，移浙西，召為宗正少卿、兵部侍郎，除右諫議大夫。
