translations.literal: He served as prefect of Jianning and Vice Transport Commissioner of Fujian, Judicial Intendant of Jiangdong, then transferred to Western Zhejiang; was summoned as Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court and Vice Minister of War, and appointed Right Remonstrance and Discussion Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Jianning and vice transport commissioner of Fujian, as judicial intendant of Jiangdong, then transferred to western Zhejiang; he was summoned as vice director of the Imperial Clan Court and vice minister of war, and appointed right remonstrance and discussion grandee.

sentences.zh: 良翰言：「以蜀漢之師下關陝，以荊、襄、韓、魏，江、淮搗青、徐，此今日大計。

translations.literal: Lianghan said: "With the armies of Shu and Han descending on Guanzhong, and with Jing, Xiang, Han, and Wei, and with the Jiang and Huai striking Qing and Xu—this is today's great strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Lianghan said, "Send the armies of Shu and Han down on Guanzhong, deploy forces through Jing, Xiang, Han, and Wei, and strike Qing and Xu from the Jiang and Huai—this is the great strategy of the day.

sentences.zh: 四川既命大臣，而荊、淮未有任責者，亦當擇重臣臨之。」

translations.literal: Since Sichuan has already been assigned a grand minister, yet Jing and Huai have no one bearing responsibility, a weighty minister should also be chosen to oversee them."
translations.idiomatic: Since a grand minister has already been assigned to Sichuan, yet no one has been charged with Jing and Huai, a weighty minister should likewise be chosen to take command there."

sentences.zh: 上稱善。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 進給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 大將成閔冒請真奉，有司坐獲譴，閤門王抃矯詔遣妄人謝顯出境，顯既抵罪，置閔與抃不問，良翰皆駁議，請正典刑。

translations.literal: Grand General Cheng Min presumptuously requested real stipends; the responsible officials were punished accordingly. Gatekeeper Wang Bian forged an edict sending the reckless man Xie Xian across the border. After Xian was convicted, Min and Bian were left unquestioned. Lianghan rejected both decisions and requested proper statutory punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Cheng Min presumptuously requested real stipends, and the responsible officials were punished accordingly. Gatekeeper Wang Bian forged an edict that sent a reckless man, Xie Xian, across the border. After Xian was convicted, Min and Bian were left unpunished. Lianghan rejected both decisions and called for proper legal punishment.

sentences.zh: 遂改禮部侍郎，不拜，以敷文閣待制提舉江州太平興國宮。

translations.literal: He was then changed to Vice Minister of Rites, did not accept the appointment, and served as Drafting Academician of the Fuwen Pavilion directing the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as vice minister of rites but declined the appointment and instead served as drafting academician of the Fuwen Pavilion, directing the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 召為太子詹事，既見，上屬以調護之責。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; once he had been received in audience, the Emperor entrusted him with the duty of nurturing and protecting the heir.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as grand mentor of the heir apparent; after audience, the emperor entrusted him with the duty of nurturing and protecting the heir.

sentences.zh: 一日，召對選德殿，出手書唐太宗與魏征論仁德功利之說，俾極陳今日所未至者。

translations.literal: One day he was summoned to audience in the Xuande Hall; the Emperor produced in his own hand the Tang Taizong and Wei Zheng discussion of benevolence, virtue, utility, and merit, and ordered him to set forth fully what had not yet been achieved today.
translations.idiomatic: One day he was summoned to audience in the Xuande Hall. The emperor produced in his own hand Taizong of Tang's exchange with Wei Zheng on benevolence, virtue, utility, and merit, and ordered him to set forth fully where the court had still fallen short.

sentences.zh: 良翰退，上疏，略曰：「仁德治之本，功利治之效，務本而效自至。

translations.literal: Lianghan withdrew and submitted a memorial, saying in summary: "Benevolence and virtue are the root of governance; utility and merit are governance's effects. Attend to the root and the effects will come of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Lianghan withdrew and submitted a memorial saying, in summary, "Benevolence and virtue are the root of governance; utility and merit are its effects. Attend to the root and the effects will follow of themselves.

sentences.zh: 今承天意，結民心，任賢能，退小人，擇將帥，收軍情，擇監司，吏久任，皆行之有未至，誠能革此八弊，則仁德無累，功利自致矣。」

translations.literal: Now receiving Heaven's mandate, binding the people's hearts, appointing the worthy and able, dismissing petty men, choosing generals and commanders, gathering military sentiment, selecting surveillance commissioners, and long tenure for officials—in all of these execution falls short. If these eight defects can truly be reformed, then benevolence and virtue will be unburdened and utility and merit will come of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Receiving Heaven's mandate, winning the people's hearts, appointing the worthy and able, dismissing petty men, choosing generals and commanders, restoring military morale, selecting surveillance commissioners, and granting officials long tenure—in all of these the court still falls short. If these eight defects can truly be reformed, benevolence and virtue will be unburdened and utility and merit will follow of themselves."

sentences.zh: 上為之嘉歎，詔兼侍講。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and sighed over it and ordered him to serve concurrently as Court Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised it warmly and ordered him to serve concurrently as court lecturer.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以疾告老，除敷文閣直學士、提舉太平宮。

translations.literal: Before long he reported illness and requested retirement; he was granted Direct Academician of the Fuwen Pavilion and was assigned to direct the Taiping Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he reported illness and requested retirement; he was granted direct academician of the Fuwen Pavilion and assigned to direct the Taiping Palace.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，特諡「獻肅」。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended, he was specially posthumously ennobled with the title "Xiansu."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong ascended the throne, he was specially granted the posthumous title "Xiansu."

sentences.zh: 杜莘老

translations.literal: Du Shenlao
translations.idiomatic: Du Shenlao

sentences.zh: 杜莘老，字起莘，眉州青神人，唐工部甫十三世孫也。

translations.literal: Du Shenlao, styled Qixin, was a native of Qingshen in Meizhou, thirteenth-generation descendant of Du Fu, Ministry of Works of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shenlao, whose style name was Qixin, was a native of Qingshen in Meizhou and a thirteenth-generation descendant of Du Fu of the Tang Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 幼歲時，方禁蘇氏文，獨喜誦習。

translations.literal: In his childhood, when Su Shi's writings were banned, he alone delighted in reciting and studying them.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth, when Su Shi's writings were banned, he alone delighted in reciting and studying them.

sentences.zh: 紹興間，第進士，以親老不赴廷對，賜同進士出身。

translations.literal: During Shaoxing he passed the jinshi examination; because his parents were aged he did not attend the palace examination and was granted jinshi by special decree.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaoxing reign he passed the jinshi examination, but because his parents were elderly he did not attend the palace examination and was granted jinshi status by special decree.

sentences.zh: 授梁山軍教授，從游者眾。

translations.literal: He was appointed Instructor of Liangshan Prefecture; many followed him in study.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed instructor at Liangshan Prefecture, and many students came to study under him.

sentences.zh: 秦檜死，魏良臣參大政，莘老疏天下利害以聞。

translations.literal: When Qin Hui died, Wei Liangchen entered major state affairs; Shenlao memorialized on the benefits and harms under Heaven to inform him.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin Hui died and Wei Liangchen entered the highest councils of state, Shenlao submitted a memorial on the benefits and harms facing the realm.

sentences.zh: 良臣薦之，主管禮、兵部架閣文字。

translations.literal: Liangchen recommended him, and he took charge of archival documents in the Ministries of Rites and War.
translations.idiomatic: Liangchen recommended him, and he was put in charge of archival documents in the ministries of rites and war.

sentences.zh: 彗星見東方，高宗下詔求言，莘老上書，論：「彗，盩氣所生，多為兵兆。

translations.literal: A comet appeared in the east; Emperor Gaozong issued an edict seeking remonstrance. Shenlao submitted a letter arguing: "Comets arise from turbulent qi and often portend warfare.
translations.idiomatic: A comet appeared in the east; Emperor Gaozong issued an edict seeking remonstrance. Shenlao submitted a letter arguing: "Comets arise from turbulent qi and often portend warfare.

sentences.zh: 國家為民息兵，而將驕卒惰，軍政不肅。

translations.literal: The state has stilled arms for the people, yet generals are arrogant and soldiers slack—military administration is not disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: The state has sought to still the arms of war for the people, yet generals are arrogant and soldiers slack, and military administration lacks discipline.

sentences.zh: 今因天戒以修人事，思患預防，莫大於此。」

translations.literal: Now, taking Heaven's warning to rectify human affairs, thinking ahead to prevent calamity—nothing is greater than this."
translations.idiomatic: To take Heaven's warning as an occasion to rectify human affairs and think ahead to prevent calamity—nothing is more urgent than this."

sentences.zh: 因陳時弊十事。

translations.literal: He thereupon set forth ten current abuses.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon set forth ten current abuses.

sentences.zh: 時應詔者眾，上命擇其議論切當推恩以勸之，後省以莘老為首，進一階，遷敕令刪定官、太常寺主簿，升博士。

translations.literal: At the time many responded to the edict; the Emperor ordered that those whose arguments were incisive and apt receive favors to encourage them. The Secretariat placed Shenlao first; he was advanced one rank, transferred to Edict and Decree Revising Officer and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and promoted to Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Many responded to the edict at the time; the emperor ordered that those whose arguments were incisive and apt receive favors as encouragement. The secretariat ranked Shenlao first; he was advanced one rank, appointed edict and decree revising officer and vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and promoted to erudite.

sentences.zh: 輪對，論：「金將敗盟，宜飭邊備，勿恃其不來，恃吾有以待之。」

translations.literal: In turn for audience he argued: "The Jin will break the covenant—border defenses should be strengthened. Do not rely on their not coming; rely on our being prepared to receive them."
translations.idiomatic: In a routine audience he argued that the Jin would break the covenant, that border defenses should be strengthened, and that the court should not rely on the enemy's staying away but on its own readiness to meet them."

sentences.zh: 上稱善再三。

translations.literal: The Emperor repeatedly praised it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly praised it.

sentences.zh: 南渡後，典秩散失，多有司所記省，至凶禮又諱不錄。

translations.literal: After the southward crossing, canonical ranks and ordinances were scattered and lost; much was recorded only in abbreviated form by the responsible offices, and ominous rites were tabooed and not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: After the court crossed south, canonical ranks and ritual ordinances were scattered and lost; much survived only in abbreviated records kept by the responsible offices, and ominous rites were deliberately omitted.

sentences.zh: 顯仁皇后崩，議禮有疑，吏皆拱手，莘老以古義裁定。

translations.literal: When Empress Xianren died, there were doubts in deliberating the rites; officials all stood with folded hands. Shenlao settled it by ancient principle.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Xianren died, doubts arose in deliberating the funeral rites and the officials all stood aside with folded hands. Shenlao settled the matter according to ancient principle.

sentences.zh: 大斂前一日，宰相傳旨問含玉之制，莘老曰：「禮院故實所不載，請以《周禮》典瑞鄭玄《注》製之，其可。」

translations.literal: On the day before the great encoffining, the chief minister relayed an order asking about the regulation for placing jade in the mouth. Shenlao said: "The Ritual Office's established precedents do not record this—I request that it be made according to the Commentary of Zheng Xuan on the Regalia section of the Rites of Zhou; that will do."
translations.idiomatic: On the day before the great encoffining, the chief minister relayed an order asking about the regulation for placing jade in the mouth. Shenlao said, "The Ritual Office's established precedents do not record this. I request that it be done according to Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Regalia section of the Rites of Zhou—that will suffice."

sentences.zh: 因立具奏，上覽之曰：「真禮官也。」

translations.literal: He immediately drafted a full memorial; the Emperor read it and said: "A true ritual officer."
translations.idiomatic: He immediately drafted a full memorial. The emperor read it and said, "A true ritual officer."

sentences.zh: 及虞祭，或謂上哀勞，欲以宰相行事。

translations.literal: When it came to the Yu sacrifice, some said the Emperor was worn with grief and labor and wished to have the chief minister perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: When it came to the Yu sacrifice, some argued that the emperor, worn with grief, wished to have the chief minister perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 莘老曰：「古今無是。」

translations.literal: Shenlao said: "There is no such thing in antiquity or the present."
translations.idiomatic: Shenlao said, "There is no such precedent in antiquity or the present."

sentences.zh: 卒正之。

translations.literal: In the end it was corrected.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the matter was corrected.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書丞，論江、淮守備，上曰：「卿言及此，憂國深矣。」

translations.literal: He was transferred to Secretariat Assistant Director; discussing Jiang and Huai defenses, the Emperor said: "When you speak of this, your concern for the state runs deep."
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to secretariat assistant director. Discussing Jiang and Huai defenses, the emperor said, "When you speak of this, your concern for the state runs deep."

sentences.zh: 擢監察御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中侍御史，入對，上曰：「知卿不畏強禦，故有此授，自是用卿矣。」

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant Censor; entering audience, the Emperor said: "Knowing that you do not fear the powerful, I therefore make this appointment—from now on I shall employ you."
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to palace attendant censor. Entering audience, the emperor said, "Knowing that you do not fear the powerful, I make this appointment because of that—from now on I shall employ you."

sentences.zh: 陳俊卿既解言職，力求去，莘老因奏事，從容曰：「多事之際，令俊卿輩在論思之地，必有補益。」

translations.literal: Chen Junqing had already resigned his remonstrance duties and earnestly sought to leave. Shenlao, while reporting on affairs, said calmly: "In these many-troubled times, keeping Junqing and his like in places of deliberation and reflection will surely be of benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Junqing had already resigned his remonstrance duties and earnestly sought to leave. While reporting on affairs, Shenlao said calmly, "In these troubled times, keeping Junqing and his like in posts of deliberation and reflection would surely be of benefit."

sentences.zh: 上以為然，俊卿乃復留。

translations.literal: The Emperor thought this correct, and Junqing then remained.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and Junqing stayed on.

sentences.zh: 金遣使致嫚書，傳欽宗凶問，請淮、漢地，指索大臣。

translations.literal: The Jin sent envoys bearing an insulting letter, transmitting news of Emperor Qinzong's death, demanding the Huai and Han territories, and naming specific grand ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin sent envoys bearing an insulting letter, transmitting news of Emperor Qinzong's death, demanding the Huai and Han territories, and naming specific grand ministers for surrender.

sentences.zh: 上決策親征，莘老疏奏贊上，且謂：「敵欺天背盟，當待以不懼，勿以小利鈍為異議所搖，諛言所惰，則人心有恃而士氣振矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor decided on a personal campaign. Shenlao memorialized in support of the Emperor and also said: "The enemy deceives Heaven and betrays the covenant—they should be met with fearlessness. Do not let petty gains dull resolve or be shaken by dissenting views and enervated by flattery—then the people's hearts will have support and military morale will rise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor decided on a personal campaign. Shenlao memorialized in support and also said: "The enemy has deceived Heaven and betrayed the covenant and should be met without fear; the court must not let petty gains dull its resolve or be shaken by dissent or enervated by flattery, and then the people's hearts will have something to rely on and military morale will rise.

sentences.zh: 宜不限早暮，延見大臣、侍從，謀議國事；

translations.literal: One should not limit early or late hours in summoning grand ministers and attendants to discuss state affairs;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor should summon grand ministers and attendants without regard to hour, morning or evening, to deliberate on state affairs;

sentences.zh: 申敕侍從、臺諫、監司、守臣，亟舉可用之才。」

translations.literal: charge attendants, censorate-remonstrance officials, surveillance commissioners, and prefectural officials to recommend promptly men of usable talent."
translations.idiomatic: and charge attendants, censorate-remonstrance officials, surveillance commissioners, and prefectural officials to recommend promptly men of usable talent."

sentences.zh: 又言：「親征有期，而禁衛才五千餘，羸老居半，至不能介胄者，願亟留聖慮。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The personal campaign has a set date, yet the Imperial Guard numbers only a little over five thousand—the weak and aged make up half, even to the point of men unable to don armor. I beg that Your Majesty's attention dwell urgently on this."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The personal campaign has a set date, yet the Imperial Guard numbers just over five thousand—the weak and aged make up half, including men unable even to don armor. I beg that Your Majesty give this urgent attention."

sentences.zh: 事皆施行。

translations.literal: All matters were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: All his recommendations were carried out.

sentences.zh: 帶御器械劉炎筦禁中市易，通北賈，大為姦利。

translations.literal: Bearer of Imperial Arms Liu Yan managed market exchange within the forbidden city, trafficking with northern merchants, and greatly profited by wicked means.
translations.idiomatic: Bearer of imperial arms Liu Yan controlled market exchange within the forbidden city, trafficked with northern merchants, and reaped enormous illicit profit.

sentences.zh: 一日，見莘老，輒及朝政，語狂悖，莘老以聞，斥監嘉州稅。

translations.literal: One day, meeting Shenlao, he promptly spoke of court affairs in reckless and rebellious language. Shenlao reported it, and he was demoted to supervise taxation in Jiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: One day, meeting Shenlao, he promptly spoke of court affairs in reckless and seditious language. Shenlao reported it, and Liu was demoted to supervise taxation in Jiazhou.

sentences.zh: 知樞密院事周麟之初請使金，及嫚書至，聞金將盛兵犯邊，乃大恐，建言不必遣使。

translations.literal: Bureau of Military Affairs Commissioner Zhou Linzhi had initially requested to serve as envoy to the Jin; when the insulting letter arrived and he heard the Jin would mass troops to violate the border, he was greatly terrified and advised that envoys need not be sent.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau of military affairs commissioner Zhou Linzhi had initially volunteered to serve as envoy to the Jin, but when the insulting letter arrived and he heard the Jin would mass troops to violate the border, he was terrified and advised that no envoy need be sent.

sentences.zh: 莘老劾麟之：「挾姦罔上，避事辭難，恐懼至於掩泣，眾有『哭殺富鄭公』之誚。」

translations.literal: Shenlao impeached Linzhi: "He harbors treachery and deceives his sovereign, shirks duty and evades hardship—his fear reached the point of covering his face and weeping. The crowd has the jeer, 'Crying the Duke of Zheng to death.'
translations.idiomatic: Shenlao impeached Linzhi, saying he harbored treachery and deceived his sovereign, shirked duty and evaded hardship, and was so terrified he covered his face and wept—the crowd mocked him with the saying, "Crying the Duke of Zheng to death."

sentences.zh: 尋與宮觀。

translations.literal: Soon he was given a palace directorship.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given a palace directorship.

sentences.zh: 疏再上，乃責瑞州。

translations.literal: After another memorial he was then demoted to Ruizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Shenlao submitted another memorial, Linzhi was demoted to Ruizhou.

sentences.zh: 幸醫承宣使王繼先怙寵干法，富浮公室，子弟直延閣，居第僭擬，別業、外帑遍畿甸，數十年無敢搖之者，聞邊警，亟輦重寶歸吳興為避敵計。

translations.literal: Favorite Physician Commissioner Wang Jixian, relying on favor, violated the law; wealth overflowed the public coffers; his sons and younger brothers held posts at the Hanlin Academy; his residence usurped princely standards; secondary estates and external treasuries spread throughout the capital region—for decades none dared shake him. Hearing border alarms, he hurriedly carted heavy treasures back to Wuxing as a plan to flee the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Favorite physician commissioner Wang Jixian, relying on imperial favor, violated the law; his wealth overflowed the public coffers; his sons and younger brothers held posts at the Hanlin Academy; his residence usurped princely standards; secondary estates and external treasuries spread throughout the capital region—and for decades none dared move against him. When he heard border alarms, he hurriedly carted heavy treasures back to Wuxing to prepare for flight from the enemy.

sentences.zh: 莘老疏其十罪，上曰：「初以太后餌其藥，稍假恩寵，不謂小人驕橫乃爾。」

translations.literal: Shenlao memorialized his ten crimes. The Emperor said: "At first, because the Empress Dowager took his medicines, I slightly extended favor—but I never thought a petty man could become so arrogant."
translations.idiomatic: Shenlao memorialized his ten crimes. The emperor said, "At first, because the empress dowager took his medicines, I extended him some favor—but I never thought a petty man could become so arrogant."

sentences.zh: 莘老曰：「繼先罪擢髮不足數，臣所奏，其大概耳。」

translations.literal: Shenlao said: "Jixian's crimes—even counting each hair would not suffice to enumerate them. What I memorialized was only the general outline."
translations.idiomatic: Shenlao said, "Jixian's crimes—even counting each hair on his head would not suffice to enumerate them. What I memorialized was only the general outline."

sentences.zh: 上作色曰：「有恩無威，有賞無罰，雖堯舜不能治天下。」

translations.literal: The Emperor changed color and said: "With favor but no authority, with rewards but no punishments—even Yao and Shun could not govern all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's expression changed and he said, "With favor but no authority, with rewards but no punishments—even Yao and Shun could not govern the realm."

sentences.zh: 詔繼先福州居住，子孫皆勒停。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jixian to reside in Fuzhou; his sons and descendants were all stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Jixian to reside in Fuzhou, and his sons and descendants were all stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 籍其貲以千萬計，詔鬻錢入御前激賞庫，專以賞將士，天下稱快。

translations.literal: His assets registered in the tens of millions; an edict ordered the sale of the proceeds into the Imperial Front Merit-Reward Treasury, devoted solely to rewarding officers and soldiers—all under Heaven rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: His assets were registered in the tens of millions; an edict ordered the proceeds sold into the imperial front merit-reward treasury to reward officers and soldiers alone, and all under Heaven rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 內侍張去為取御馬院西兵二百髡其頂，都人異之，口語籍籍。

translations.literal: Palace attendant Zhang Quwei took two hundred Western soldiers from the Imperial Horse Yard and shaved their heads; the capital's people thought it strange and gossip spread.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Zhang Quwei took two hundred Western soldiers from the Imperial Horse Yard and shaved their heads; the people of the capital thought it strange and gossip spread widely.

sentences.zh: 莘老彈治，上疑其未審，不樂。

translations.literal: Shenlao impeached and prosecuted him; the Emperor doubted the facts were not verified and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Shenlao impeached him, but the emperor doubted the matter had not yet been verified and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 莘老執奏不已，竟罷去為御馬院，致仕，而莘老亦以直顯謨閣知遂寧府。

translations.literal: Shenlao persisted in memorializing without cease; in the end Quwei was dismissed to the Imperial Horse Yard and retired, while Shenlao too was made Direct Academician of the Zhixianmoge and prefect of Suining.
translations.idiomatic: Shenlao persisted in memorializing without cease; in the end Quwei was dismissed to the Imperial Horse Yard and retired, while Shenlao too was made direct academician of the Zhixianmoge and appointed prefect of Suining.

sentences.zh: 給事中金安節、中書舍人劉珙封還制書，改司農少卿，尋請外，仍與遂寧。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Jin Anjie and Drafting Official Liu Yu returned the sealed edicts; Shenlao was changed to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, and soon requested an outside post—but was still sent to Suining.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising censor Jin Anjie and drafting official Liu Yu returned the sealed edicts in protest; Shenlao was reassigned as vice director of the ministry of revenue, and when he soon requested an outside post he was still sent to Suining.

sentences.zh: 始莘老自蜀造朝，不以家行。

translations.literal: From the first, when Shenlao came from Shu to court, he did not bring his household.
translations.idiomatic: From the beginning, when Shenlao came from Shu to court, he traveled without his household.

sentences.zh: 高宗聞其清修獨處，甚重之，一日因對，褒諭曰：「聞卿出蜀，即蒲團、紙帳如僧然，難及也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong heard of his pure conduct living alone and greatly valued him. One day during audience he praised him, saying: "I hear that when you left Shu you had only a meditation cushion and paper canopy like a monk—hard to match."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong heard of his pure solitary living and greatly valued him. One day during audience he praised him, saying, "I hear that when you left Shu you had only a meditation cushion and paper canopy, like a monk—hard to match."

sentences.zh: 未幾，遂擢用。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted and employed.

sentences.zh: 莘老官中都久，知公論所予奪，姦蠹者皆得其根本脈絡，嘗歎曰：「臺諫當論天下第一事，若有所畏，姑言其次，是欺其心不敬其君者也。」

translations.literal: Shenlao long served in the capital and knew what public opinion granted and denied; those who were wicked parasites—he grasped their roots and arteries. He once sighed and said: "The censorate and remonstrance offices should discuss the foremost matter under Heaven. If one has fears and speaks only of secondary matters, that is deceiving one's heart and not revering one's lord."
translations.idiomatic: Shenlao served long in the capital and knew what public opinion granted and denied; for wicked parasites he grasped their roots and full extent. He once sighed and said, "The censorate and remonstrance offices should discuss the foremost matter under Heaven. If one has fears and speaks only of secondary matters, that is deceiving one's heart and failing to revere one's lord."

sentences.zh: 及任言責，極言無隱，取眾所指目者悉擊去，聲振一時，都人稱骨鯁敢言者必曰杜殿院云。

translations.literal: When he bore the duty of remonstrance, he spoke to the utmost without concealment, striking down all those the crowd pointed at. His reputation shook the age; when the capital's people spoke of the blunt-spoken who dared speak out, they always said "Director Du of the Censorate."
translations.idiomatic: When he bore the duty of remonstrance, he spoke openly without concealment, striking down all those the crowd singled out. His reputation shook the age, and when the people of the capital spoke of blunt-spoken men who dared remonstrate, they always said, "Director Du of the censorate, they say."

sentences.zh: 治郡，課績為諸州最。

translations.literal: Governing prefectures, his performance ratings ranked highest among all prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: As a prefect, his performance ratings ranked highest among all prefectures.

sentences.zh: 孝宗受禪，莘老進三議，曰：定國是、修內政、養根本。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong received the abdication, Shenlao offered three counsels: settle the national purpose, repair internal government, and nurture the foundations.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong received the abdication, Shenlao offered three counsels: settle the national purpose, repair internal government, and nurture the foundations.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: Soon he died at age fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 論曰：黃洽渾厚有守，應辰學術精醇，尤稱骨鯁。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Huang Qia was simple and solid with integrity; Yingchen's learning was refined and pure, and he was especially called blunt-spoken.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Huang Qia was simple and solid with integrity; Yingchen's learning was refined and pure, and he was especially renowned for bluntness.

sentences.zh: 十朋、吳芾、良翰、莘老相繼在臺府，歷詆姦幸，直言無隱，皆事上忠而自信篤，足以當大任者，惜不盡其用焉。

translations.literal: Shipeng, Wu Fei, Lianghan, and Shenlao served in succession in the censorate and remonstrance offices, repeatedly denouncing favored scoundrels, speaking directly without concealment—all loyal in serving their lord and firm in self-confidence, men enough to bear great responsibility, yet it is lamentable that their capacities were not fully used.
translations.idiomatic: Shipeng, Wu Fei, Lianghan, and Shenlao served in succession in the censorate and remonstrance offices, repeatedly denouncing favored scoundrels and speaking without concealment—all loyal in serving their lords and firm in self-confidence, men fit to bear great responsibility, yet it is lamentable that their capacities were not fully used.
